323afe83d1cfb6b6: WASHINGTON, Oct 24 — Iran has “substantially increased” its efforts to target Americans in the Middle East and beyond, US national intelligence chief Jay Clayton warned on Friday.
The warning comes after Washington ordered non-essential US embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia this week, following increasing attacks from Yemen’s Houthis.
The kingdom has come under near-daily attacks this month from the Iran-backed group, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the kingdom’s deadliest in years.
“We have received intelligence that Iran has substantially increased efforts to target US personnel,” Clayton said in a memo sent to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, according to a US official.
“The lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against US citizens have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries,” said the memo, which was first reported by Axios.
Washington previously ordered non-essential staff to leave the Gulf ahead of the start of its war against Iran and again in July before US President Donald Trump called off a new wave of strikes.
The US official said: “When it comes to our staffing at embassies, we constantly evaluate new information about the security environment.”
“The threat of Houthi attacks and of Iranian terror plots targeting US officials are informing our decisions,” the official added.
Trump suggested on Friday that the US might launch renewed military operations against Iran.
“We may do another little Epic Fury” Trump said, referring to the US name for its attacks on Iran. He did not give any indication on timing.
The conflict began in late February with US-Israeli attacks on Iran, killing the country’s supreme leader, along with senior military commanders. — AFP
3a6a609851bbcaaa: KULAI, Oct 24 — The National Registration Department (JPN) has issued 275,785 new-generation MyKad nationwide since its launch on Sept 17 until Oct 20, with Johor recording the highest number at 31,392 cards.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the figures reflected a positive response from the public to the new-generation MyKad, which comes with enhanced security features.
He said the new-generation MyKad incorporates 53 security features, compared with 23 in the previous version, including a transparent window, QR code, ultraviolet features, hologram and microtext.
The enhancements were introduced to ensure the identity card’s security features remained relevant to technological advancements, following about 12 years of use of the previous MyKad generation.
“JPN has taken steps to further upgrade the security features. That is why we call it the new-generation MyKad,” he said.

“Johor recorded the highest number, with 31,392 cards issued, followed by Kuala Lumpur with 29,601, Selangor (26,736), Sarawak (25,642) and Sabah (22,523),” he told a press conference after officiating the 78th National Registration Day celebration and the launch of the Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School initiatives at the Kampung Melayu Sedenak Multipurpose Hall here today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the public need not rush to replace their MyKad, as JPN had assured that the supply of cards was sufficient to meet demand.

He said about 24 million existing MyKads were currently in circulation, while JPN received an average of 200,000 applications a month for various purposes, including new identity cards, replacements for damaged cards and MyKad issuance to those turning 18.

He said possession of a MyKad was becoming increasingly important due to various government initiatives requiring its use, including purchases of petrol and cooking oil, as well as the redemption of Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA).

“We do not have any projections. We will continue as usual and serve the public. What matters is ensuring that the card supply is sufficient to meet demand from those who choose to switch to the new-generation MyKad,” he said. — Bernama
f6cdd0df83ad95e7: REMBAU: Malaysia is prepared to provide any form of assistance to Indonesia in tackling transboundary haze, including seeking support from Gulf countries if necessary.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia understood the difficulties faced by Indonesia in managing extensive forest fires in areas far from its borders.
He said he would contact his Indonesian counterpart, Arrmanatha Christiawan Nasir, soon to discuss the assistance required.

"I also agreed with United Arab Emirates Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah Zayed Al Nahyan yesterday when he said that if assistance was needed, he was prepared to work with other countries to provide it.

"If Indonesia requires assistance, I will raise the matter with my counterparts in the Gulf countries to provide whatever help is needed," he told reporters after presenting Deepavali contributions to recipients in the Rantau state constituency at Dewan Orang Ramai Rantau here today.
Mohamad said Malaysia could not remain silent as forest fires in Indonesia also affected neighbouring countries, but any assistance operation would need to take safety considerations into account.
The Rembau member of Parliament said firefighting operations faced major challenges because the fires were located deep in remote areas, while thick haze had also reduced visibility.
He said developed countries such as Canada and the United States had also experienced forest fires, including those in Los Angeles that claimed many lives.

"It is easy for us to talk about it here, but imagine if the fires were 1,000km or even 500km from residential areas. There would be no other option but to use aircraft. However, aircraft would also be unable to carry out firefighting operations because of limited visibility," he said.

Meanwhile, Mohamad said Malaysia was prepared to provide humanitarian assistance to Yemen following discussions with Yemen's Foreign Affairs and Expatriates Minister, Dr Afrah Abdulaziz Al-Zouba, yesterday.

He also expressed hope that the civil war in Yemen could be brought to an end, saying the conflict had brought no benefits to the country's people and had left 22 million people bearing its consequences, including many facing starvation.
"Malaysia has expressed its sympathy and is prepared to participate in any relief mission or provide assistance.
"We also call on the parties with interests in the conflict from outside Yemen to come to the negotiating table so that the Yemeni people can enjoy a peaceful and prosperous life," he said.
a709014d8cb9d474: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Bursa Malaysia is likely to trend upwards next week, with the benchmark index expected to trade within the 1,600-1,620 range amid a recovery in investors’ risk appetite, said an analyst.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng expects bargain hunting to intensify as investors take advantage of increasingly attractive valuations.
However, elevated crude oil prices, geopolitical uncertainties and persistent foreign selling could trigger intermittent volatility, he added.

“Overall, we anticipate the FBM KLCI to trade within the 1,600-1,620 range next week, with a mildly positive bias supported by selective accumulation of fundamentally sound stocks,” Thong told Bernama.
He added that Malaysia’s resilient economic fundamentals and relatively contained inflation should continue to underpin corporate earnings prospects.
Meanwhile, Thong said the recent correction has brought selected blue chip stocks to more attractive valuations, particularly within the banking, plantation and utilities sectors.

For the week just ended, the local bourse traded mostly lower, in tandem with most regional markets, tracking Wall Street performance due to concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) investment sustainability
On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 3.80 points to 1,611.56 from 1,607.76 a week earlier.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index added 1.18 points to 11,993.45, the FBM Top 100 Index increased 10.84 points to 11,797.61, and the FBM Emas Shariah Index garnered 23.70 points to 11,943.57.
The FBM ACE Index dipped 84.93 points to 5,346.14 and the FBM Mid 70 Index decreased 55.61 points to 17,170.33.

By sector, the Energy Index advanced 13.67 points to 834.67, the Plantation Index gained 44.60 points to 8,677.48, and the Industrial Products and Services Index climbed 2.61 points to 175.4. The Financial Services Index tumbled 97.50 points to 18,654.32.
Weekly turnover fell to 14.21 billion units worth RM12.55 billion from 16.41 billion units worth RM15.57 billion in the previous week.
The Main Market volume decreased to 7.68 billion units valued at RM11.15 billion versus 9.58 billion units valued at RM13.89 billion previously.
Warrants turnover declined to 4.15 billion units worth RM514.80 million against 4.23 billion units worth RM573.41 million a week ago.
The ACE Market volume slipped to 2.37 billion units valued at RM889.53 million from 2.60 billion units valued at RM1.01 billion in the previous week. — Bernama

df98c5c2c045fc99: Established under the Franco dictatorship, the lunchtime ritual is in decline but all is not lost A little before lunchtime each working day across Spain, evidence of one of the lingering, if less notorious, legacies of the Franco dictatorship is carefully traced in chalk, marker pen and printer ink. Beckoning to hungry workers from blackboards, whiteboards and pieces of paper hastily taped to windows, the competitively priced menú del día, or daily set-price lunch, has been part of everyday Spanish life for more than half a century. 10629099d2e40e38: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The ringgit is expected to trade within a narrow range of RM4.07 to RM4.08 against the US dollar next week as investors monitor the outcome of the US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting scheduled for October 27-28.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said investors will also look for clues on the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy direction from the FOMC statement and subsequent press conference, with markets expecting the Fed funds rate to remain unchanged at 3.75 to 4.00 per cent.

“Essentially, the Fed’s assessment of inflation and the prevailing market conditions surrounding artificial intelligence investments and equity valuations will be critical elements in shaping market confidence.
“More importantly, it is whether there will be any change in tone regarding the current monetary policy stance and the outlook for current and future inflation rates,” he told Bernama.
Hence, he said the US dollar-ringgit pair is expected to trade within a narrow range.
Meanwhile, on a Friday-to-Friday basis, the ringgit eased against the greenback to 4.0835/0875 from 4.0795/0835 a week earlier.
The local currency traded mostly lower against a basket of other major currencies during the week.

It inched down vis-a-vis the Japanese yen to 2.6076/6103 from 2.5831/5895 on the previous Friday and depreciated against the British pound to 5.4633/4687 from 5.4396/4449, but it gained versus the euro to 4.5735/5780 from 4.5911/5956 a week earlier.
The ringgit traded mostly higher against Asean currencies.

It climbed vis-a-vis the Thai baht to 12.0985/1154 from 12.2101/2268 a week earlier, inched up against the Indonesian rupiah to 225.8/226.1 from 226.3/226.6 and went up against the Philippine peso to 6.42/6.43 from 6.48/6.49
The local note, however, declined versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1952/1986 from 3.1889/1922 at the end of last week. — Bernama
212f4be757766e73: KUCHING: Pas will likely contest three state seats in the coming Sarawak election, says the Islamist party's state chief, Mohammad Arifiriazul Paijo.
He said the party was eyeing Semariang, Sebuyau and Beting Marau, although the final decision rested with the Pas central leadership.
He said Sarawak Pas had proposed contesting the three seats and that its election machinery in the areas was ready.
Arifiriazul said the party was also considering contesting another seat in northern Sarawak, either within the Bintulu or Sibuti parliamentary constituency.
However, he said Pas was not ready to disclose which seat it was considering.
7f45214c9193d736: PHILLIP ISLAND (Australia): Marc Marquez stormed home first from pole in the Australian MotoGP sprint race on Saturday to seize control of the world championship from Jorge Martin who crashed out challenging him for the lead.
The reigning seven-time world champion, who dominated qualifying, had too much power in his Ducati to surge to the chequered flag ahead of his brother Alex in the 13-lap contest.
Victory put him 10 points clear of fellow Spaniard Martin in the standings ahead of the final MotoGP ever around the waterfront Phillip Island circuit on Sunday.
Martin, who started from fourth under dark clouds but with the rain staying away, took the lead on lap three in a ding-dong battle with his rival.
But he lost control on lap eight while challenging for the lead once again to put a massive dent in his championship ambitions.
"It was a tight battle," said Marquez. "Of course, I gave everything. I was aggressive, and he (Martin) was faster than me.
"But just I tried to defend in the best way possible. Both of us we are riding to the limit. Both of us, we deserve the victory because we are pushing a lot.
"But, you know, racing is like it is."
His brother Alex, who started second, filled an all-Ducati podium with Fabio Di Giannantonio.
Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi, who won the MotoGP last week in Indonesia, was fourth to remain third in the standings, 50 points behind Marquez.
Pedro Acosta (KTM) came fifth and Ai Ogura (Aprilia) sixth.
Marc Marquez held the line to be first at the opening corner with Martin up to second with Johann Zarco third and it stayed that way at the end of lap one.
Martin was pressing hard and he took the lead on lap three as the race became a dogfight between the two championship leaders as they pulled clear of the field.
A big mistake from Martin running wide on lap five opened the door again for Marquez, with the lead changing hands several times as they battled for supremacy.
But Martin pushed too much and sensationally lost control on lap eight, skidding out to end his race.
Phillip Island has been a staple on the calendar since 1997 but the Australian race is moving next year to a street circuit in Adelaide. - AFP
84a4415ba3b078ba: SHAH ALAM, Oct 24 — Edaran Otomobil Nasional Bhd (EON) has strengthened its after-sales services for customers with the launch of its first vehicle body and paint repair hub in Glenmarie here.

Spanning 41,508 square feet, the centre is equipped with 39 work bays, three paint-mixing rooms and four spray booths to meet the repair and restoration needs of various vehicle brands under EON, including Proton, Mitsubishi, Audi and smart electric vehicles. It is also expected to accommodate Proton e.Mas vehicles in the future.

EON chief executive officer Akkbar Danial said the opening of the centre demonstrated the company’s commitment to providing a more comprehensive vehicle ownership experience, as the company’s relationship with customers does not end once a new vehicle leaves the showroom.
“Every point of interaction throughout the ownership journey is an opportunity for us to deliver value, build trust and create meaningful experiences.

“This commitment is being realised through the hub, which adheres to EON’s procedures and processes to ensure that after-sales services are comprehensive and of high quality,” he said at a press conference held in conjunction with the hub’s launch yesterday.
Earlier, the official opening ceremony was officiated by DRB-HICOM Bhd group chief operating officer for corporate services Datuk Jezilee Mohamad Ramli.
Akkbar said the vehicle body and paint repair hub was equipped with modern repair technology and supported by a team of trained professionals.
“The centre also accepts accident repair claims from all insurance companies, thereby providing customers with better access to its services.
“Besides offering a seamless repair and painting process, vehicles are returned in optimal condition while maintaining safety, quality and aesthetic standards,” he said.

The opening of the hub would strengthen EON’s after-sales ecosystem and support the company’s brand promise, “Passion Drives Possibilities”, by ensuring that service interactions go beyond customer expectations, he said.
“With more than four decades of experience in the country’s automotive industry, EON continues to transform itself into a more customer-centric mobility partner.
“Besides connecting communities through mobility, we aim to provide convenient and reliable solutions for vehicle care needs,” he said.
Akkbar said the company also planned to explore opportunities to expand the network of hubs to strategic locations in other states in the future.
“This move will enable EON to leverage its existing network while enhancing service accessibility and providing better support to customers across its automotive portfolio,” he said. — Bernama
1578cbfe83b7e133: GEORGE TOWN: Berita Harian (BH) and Harian Metro (HM) have been recognised by Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka (DBP) for their contributions to promoting and strengthening the use of Bahasa Melayu.
Both publications received the Hadiah Citra Bahasa Sahabat DBP 2026 at the launch of the 2026 National Language Month at Padang Kota here.
BH group editor Zulkifli Jalil and HM group editor Husain Jahit received the awards.

The Hadiah Citra Bahasa Sahabat DBP recognises organisations from the public and private sectors, as well as non-governmental organisations, for their contributions and commitment to promoting the national language.
Recipients receive a certificate of appreciation and RM5,000 in collaboration funding to organise literary bazaar activities.
The ceremony also saw the presentation of the Hadiah Citra Bahasa 2026, which recognises high achievement in Bahasa Melayu proficiency assessments. Recipients received RM3,000.

The Anugerah Ikon Bahasa 2026 was presented to lyricist and writer Datuk Habsah Hassan, professional emcee Terence Joseph Dunn and Penang Mufti Associate Professor Datuk Dr Mohd Suki Othman for their contributions to upholding the national language.
Each recipient received RM2,000, a certificate of appreciation and books published by DBP.
The awards were presented by Education Ministry deputy director-general (Professional Development Sector) Datuk Amzan Abd Malek.
Husain said HM would continue to champion Bahasa Melayu at both national and international levels.
He said the recognition reflected the newspaper's continued commitment to promoting the national language through its media platforms and initiatives.
"We are proud to receive this award, as it shows that HM continues to be recognised," he said.
Husain said HM had recently organised a pantun competition in collaboration with DBP and DRB-HICOM to promote the Malay language and preserve its literary heritage.
He said pantun, a traditional Malay poetic form, remained an important part of Bahasa Melayu and a valuable medium for nurturing public appreciation of the language.
Meanwhile, Zulkifli said young people should use Bahasa Melayu wisely and preserve its integrity as a reflection of their identity.
He said the tendency to modify the language on social media to suit individual preferences should not come at the expense of its proper use.
"If we look at social media, much of our language has been modified to suit their tastes. However, we should preserve the national language because it reflects our identity," he said.
Zulkifli also highlighted the role of newspapers in helping young people improve their language proficiency, particularly in grammar and writing.
He encouraged students to read newspapers, including BH, the New Straits Times (NST) and other publications circulated in schools.
"Newspapers use language that is proper and somewhat academic. I hope students will return to reading newspapers, especially to learn from the grammar used," he said.
He said regular exposure to well-written news articles could help students better understand Bahasa Melayu and use it appropriately in everyday communication.

dc82df442ee048f8: KAJANG: A man who was reported missing by his family five days ago was found dead in a car at a supermarket car park in Jalan Impian Mahkota last night.
District police chief assistant commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said police received a report about the discovery of the car at 11.29pm.
"Initial investigations found a man, believed to be in his 50s, lying unconscious in the driver's seat of a Perodua Axia.
"The engine was off and the car was locked from the inside," he said.
He said police sought the assistance of Fire and Rescue Department personnel to open the car door before medical personnel from Kajang Hospital examined the victim and pronounced him dead.
He said police received a missing person report last Tuesday after the man's family members were unable to contact him.
"Preliminary investigations have so far found no foul play at the scene or on the deceased. The case has been classified as a sudden death report (SDR).
"Further investigations are ongoing to determine the cause of the incident and his death," he said in a statement today.
Those with information about the incident is urged to contact investigating officer Inspector Shisheewady Ruzani at 016-856 5670 or the nearest police station.
Earlier, several photographs went viral showing police and Fire and Rescue Department personnel examining a parked car near a supermarket.
Following this, several social media users claimed that the man inside the car was their family member who had been reported missing five days earlier and was found at the location.
The man and the car were found about 15 minutes from where he allegedly lived.

5a866d923ec536ea: PETALING JAYA: Amanah communications director Khalid Samad has urged Pakatan Harapan to go solo in the upcoming Melaka polls and the next general election (GE16), particularly to take on Umno and PAS.

With a Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional pact confirmed for Melaka and appearing increasingly likely for GE16, Khalid said going solo would allow for a united front to be presented to take on the Umno-PAS alliance.
"This approach would allow PH to offer policies and candidates whose principles are clear, without any confusion about political manoeuvering or cooperation with other parties.
"At the same time, this stand can strengthen the identity of PH's struggle while boosting accountability and people's confidence in the coalition's struggle," he said in a statement.

Khalid added that PH must make clear that it rejects Umno's money politics and PAS's autocracy, while explaining to voters, especially the Malays, about the detriments of these two political practices.

"They need to realise that there is a third option in Malay politics offered by the Malays in PH - whether in Amanah, PKR or DAP - who champion good governance, efficient service, and the people's wellbeing.
"Rejecting Umno and PAS should be PH's main slogan in the Melaka polls and in GE16," the former MP said.
PH and BN are currently allies in the government, but the latter teamed up with PN in the recent Negeri Sembilan polls, and secured a two-thirds majority.
Earlier this week, BN chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi confirmed that the Umno-led coalition will join forces with PN once again in the Melaka polls.
He said BN will contest 21 of the 28 seats in the Melaka legislative assembly, while PAS and its PN allies will vie for the remaining seven.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka polls. Nominations will be held on Oct 31, with early voting set for Nov 10.
799db4e77934ba71: KUALA LUMPUR: Growing up with poor vision, Wong Kar Gee spent years competing against able-bodied athletes before discovering para-sports,
Now after winning an Asian Para Games gold in Nagoya, Japan on Wednesday. the 35-year-old Sabahan believes he is on course for a Paralympic medal.

Kar Gee triumphed in the men's long jump T12 after leaping 6.74 metres. He posted his winning distance on his opening attempt, before clearing 6.60m, 6.47m, 6.36m, 6.39m, and 6.40m on his remaining jumps.
Uzbekistan's Sevinchbek Khusanov finished second (6.54m) while Japan's Daiki Ishiyama was third (6.48m).
For Kar Gee, it was an improvement as he claimed silver in the same event at the 2018 Jakarta edition. He missed the last Games, in 2022 in Hangzhou due to injury.
"I'm glad to finally compete in the Asian Para Games again and win gold," he said.

Kar Gee's journey into para-sports began only in 2017. "I was studying in a normal school and competing with able-bodied athletes until 2016. It was only in 2017 that I learnt about para-sports and decided to make the move," he said.
Diagnosed with Stargardt disease at the age of eight, Kar Gee had impaired vision but said his family never treated him differently.
"I basically grew up like any normal child. My parents and family never treated me differently," he said.
However, Kar Gee's eyesight posed challenges when he pursued tertiary studies in Australia, as he struggled to read textbooks.
"I had problems reading books. I told my mother, and she asked me to return home and focus on the family business," he said.
Back in Sabah, Kar Gee trains at least once a day while running a farm that includes poultry, prawns and hydroponics.
The entrepreneur credits his family for enabling him to balance his sporting ambitions, business responsibilities and life with his wife and one-year-old daughter, Charlotte.
"I can focus on my sports, work, manage my farm, as well as my family because I'm blessed with family members who can handle things without me. It gives me the space to do all these things," he said.
For now, there is a gold medal to celebrate. Kar Gee said he would mark his Nagoya triumph with a family dinner alongside relatives and friends when he returns home.

Kar Gee finished fourth in the long jump T12 at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, missing the podium by just three centimetres with a jump of 6.85m behind Argentina's Fernando Vazquez who took bronze (6.88m).
He believes his latest success will give him the momentum to challenge for a medal at the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics.
"I believe this gold medal can bring me closer to the podium at the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics. I believe I will be able to improve my jumps for LA 2028," said Kar Gee.

7c3ad78b18a763f6: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The family of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died earlier this month while under the custody of the Cheras district police, brought their fight for justice directly to the prime minister's doorstep this morning, demanding an independent and transparent inquiry into the circumstances surrounding his death.

Accompanied by legal counsel from rights group Lawyers for Liberty (LFL), the 42-year-old deceased's family arrived at Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's private residence in Bandar Sungai Long, gathering at the entrance before security personnel ushered them into the compound to deliver a formal protest memorandum to the prime minister's representative, NST reported.

The memorandum, handed over by Noorizwan's younger brother Nooranis Zulkefly, expressed profound alarm over unexplained physical injuries documented during the post-mortem examination, urging Putrajaya to intervene directly to prevent an institutional cover-up.

Pathologists at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) in Cheras confirmed that while the post-mortem detected no structural trauma to internal organs, Noorizwan's body bore multiple external contusions and injuries.

The formal medical cause of death remains uncertified and has been officially recorded as "pending laboratory analysis" while the Chemistry Department conducts specialised toxicological and histopathological tests.
Noorizwan was arrested by Cheras police personnel on Sept 19 under Section 39A(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, along with allegations of burglary and theft under the Penal Code.

Following 11 days in police lock-up, his physical condition deteriorated sharply, prompting authorities to transfer him to HCTM on Sept 30, where medical staff pronounced him dead in the early hours of Oct 1.

The family's petition follows public remarks by Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus, who defended the custodial administration by insisting officers followed standard operating procedures to the letter before the detainee took ill.
Fadil had publicly noted that Noorizwan held 44 prior criminal records, mainly related to narcotics and property theft, and had confessed to multiple break-ins in the Cheras district.

Bukit Aman's specialised Criminal Investigation and Deaths in Custody Unit (USJKT) has since expanded its internal affairs investigation, questioning 78 witnesses ranging from police personnel and medical specialists to legal aid representatives and the victim's immediate family.
76ecef75ca27fa96: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — National squash player S. Sivasangari moved within one win of clinching the Silicon Valley Open 2026 title after reaching the final in Redwood City, California, on Friday.
The third seed fought back from a game down to oust India’s Anahat Singh 5-11, 11-6, 11-4, 11-7 in 37 minutes in a rematch of the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games final.
Sivasangari, who retained the women’s singles gold medal at the Asian Games in Japan last month, will determine the title against Egypt’s eighth seed Farida Mohamed in the final later today.
Farida made it to the final as she prevailed against seventh seed and home player Marina Stefanoni 11-3, 4-11, 11-6, 6-11, 11-8.

The victory put the world No. 4 Sivasangari through to her second consecutive final at the tournament, giving her a chance to make amends for last year’s 10-12, 11-4, 4-11, 4-11 defeat to American Olivia Weaver.
The women’s category at the Silicon Valley Open offers total prize money of USD143,500 (about RM585,637). — Bernama
125f6f78ac518111: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional (BN) has rejected Pas's request for two additional seats in next month's Melaka state election, with its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi saying the coalition would honour its existing agreement with the party and its political allies.
Zahid said BN had agreed to allow Perikatan Nasional (PN) to contest seven seats not being contested by BN, leaving the coalition to decide how to distribute them among its component parties.

"I have also heard about attempts to negotiate for additional seats, but we already have a 'baiah' or pledge. We have an agreement that they would be given the opportunity to contest seven seats not contested by BN, and we leave it to them to distribute the seats among the component parties in PN," he said.
9297bc4509cdc327: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Josiah Hogan believes all actors should be given equal opportunities to demonstrate their acting abilities, rather than having roles allocated based primarily on popularity.
The 40-year-old actor said that given sufficient room to perform, an actor could deliver a performance that exceeds expectations.

Referring to his own experience of rarely being a production’s first choice, Josiah said he had worked hard to prove his capabilities, as demonstrated by his portrayal of SAC Kamal in the film Takluk 2: Op Daulat.
“I am often the second, third or fourth choice for a role. Even for SAC Kamal, I was the fourth choice, but my scene with Datuk Eman Manan went viral.

“We do not necessarily have to cast actors whose schedules are packed (popular actors). We can also consider those who are available, because an actor who is less busy may be more focused and deliver a much better performance,” he told reporters after the pre-launch of Takluk 2: Op Daulat here recently.
Josiah said a similar situation was common in Hollywood, where actors who were not the first choice had managed to create magic on screen, turning films into major hits.
Actor Josiah Hogan after an interview with Bernama at the pre-launch of ‘Takluk 2: Op Daulat’ at Wisma Pertahanan recently. — Bernama pic

Sharing his views on the craft of acting, he said the key to successfully portraying a character lay in an actor’s ability to understand the character’s mood and demeanour when delivering lines, rather than merely memorising the dialogue.

“As actors, the challenge lies in understanding a character and switching according to the situation. When we focus too much on the dialogue, we sometimes forget the character’s own mannerisms,” he said.

Directed by Zulkarnain Azhar, the film is inspired by the 2013 Lahad Datu incursion and Ops Daulat, during which Malaysian security forces defended the country’s sovereignty. It is a continuation of Takluk: Lahad Datu, which was released in 2024.
Takluk 2: Op Daulat, scheduled to hit cinemas on November 26, also stars Syafiq Kyle, Datuk Remy Ishak, Kamal Adli and Sara Ali. — Bernama
15d6442634660027: PALANGKARAYA (Indonesia), Oct 24 — Hundreds of students protested late Friday in Indonesia’s Palangkaraya, demanding the government do more to tackle a wildfire crisis that has shrouded their city and the wider region in toxic haze for months.

The students, many wearing surgical masks, gathered under an eerily orange sky with severely reduced visibility and waved banners urging authorities to declare a national emergency to free up more aid.

“The officials are morons, yet they get fantastic perks while the lives of the common people are tragic,” read one protest placard nailed to a wall outside the office of the governor of Central Kalimantan — an Indonesian province on the island of Borneo where the fires are taking place.
The demonstrators sang the Indonesia Pusaka patriotic song and engaged in light skirmishes with police.
No injuries or arrests were reported and as night fell, the protesters cleared up their trash before dispersing peacefully.

“We call upon the Central Kalimantan provincial government to state clearly that it is unable to mitigate this disaster, so that the situation may be officially designated a national disaster,” protest leader Yuyun Sanjaya told the crowd.
“How is it possible that such thick, dense smoke is being inhaled by helpless elderly people and newborn infants, and the government simply lets it happen?”
Wildfires have burned more than 1.9 million hectares in the nine months to September, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas — a figure the government has not confirmed or denied.
The resulting haze has sickened hundreds of thousands in Indonesia and reached as far as Malaysia, Singapore and East Timor.
Amid diplomatic objections from neighbouring countries, patience has also been running thin at home, with sporadic anti-government protests.
On Thursday, Indonesian school children prayed for rain on Java island, where fires have also ravaged several regencies and conservation areas. — AFP
2b0de589b549241f: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has instructed police to conduct a thorough, transparent and uncompromising investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly while in police custody.
Anwar said he had taken note of the presence of Noorizwan's family, who had come to submit an appeal to him today, and expressed his condolences over the death.
He said he understood the grief and anxiety faced by the family, who were awaiting answers about the circumstances surrounding Noorizwan's death.

"I have taken note of the presence of the family of the late Noorizwan Zulkefly, 42, who came to submit an appeal letter to me today. I am deeply saddened by his death and understand the grief and anxiety of the family, who are awaiting answers," he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar said he was scheduled to attend several engagements in Melaka today and had therefore delegated an officer to receive the letter and listen directly to the issues raised by the family.
He said he had also contacted Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail to obtain further information about the case.

"I have also contacted the Inspector-General of Police to obtain further information about this case and stressed that the investigation must be conducted thoroughly, transparently and without compromise, with developments in the investigation communicated to the family," he said.
Noorizwan's family earlier submitted a memorandum to Anwar at his house in Bandar Sungai Long this morning, appealing for his intervention in the case.

The family, accompanied by Lawyers for Liberty, called for immediate action and justice following his death while in detention at the Cheras district police headquarters, where he had been held since Sept 19.
Noorizwan died at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz on Oct 1 after being taken there for treatment the previous day.
His preliminary post-mortem report stated that he had sustained multiple bodily injuries.
The family is seeking answers about the circumstances surrounding his death and has called for a thorough investigation into the matter.
346822a1c7bdd55c: GEORGE TOWN: Bahasa Melayu perlu diperkasakan dalam dunia digital menerusi penghasilan kandungan kreatif dan berilmu bagi menarik minat generasi muda untuk menggunakannya, sekali gus memartabatkan bahasa kebangsaan.

Menteri Pendidikan, Fadhlina Sidek, berkata mereka yang lahir pada 2010 hingga 2024 atau generasi alpha, memperoleh pendedahan bahasa bukan sahaja melalui buku teks dan bilik darjah, malah menerusi video, permainan digital, animasi, muzik, kandungan penstriman dan interaksi dalam talian.

“Saya percaya bahasa Melayu mempunyai masa hadapan yang cerah, sekiranya kita berani mengubah pendekatan dan memperluas ruang penggunaannya. Kita tidak boleh sekadar meminta generasi muda mencintai bahasa Melayu.

“Kita perlu membawa bahasa Melayu ke dalam dunia digital mereka (alpha) melalui kandungan bermutu, animasi kreatif, permainan pendidikan, video pendek yang berilmu, penerbitan elektronik dan aplikasi berasaskan teknologi terkini,” katanya pada Majlis Pelancaran Bulan Bahasa Kebangsaan 2026 Peringkat Kebangsaan di Padang Kota Lama, hari ini.
Teks ucapannya dibacakan Timbalan Ketua Pengarah Pendidikan (Sektor Pembangunan Profesionalisme) Amzan Abd Malek.

Fadhlina berkata, kerajaan turut memberikan penekanan kepada pembangunan teknologi digital dan kecerdasan buatan (AI) dalam Belanjawan Madani 2027, khususnya komitmen kerajaan untuk menggembleng sumber kementerian, agensi dan institusi pendidikan bagi menyumbang data bahasa digital yang sahih dan beranotasi kepada Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka (DBP).

Beliau berkata, kerjasama Kementerian Pendidikan (KPM) dengan DBP melahirkan 259 Munsyi Remaja menerusi Program Pembinaan Munsyi Remaja, selain membina 1,924 Munsyi Siswa dan 970 Munsyi Muda, di samping peranan lebih 500 orang Munsyi Dewan di seluruh negara.

Menurutnya, KPM melalui DBP turut memperluas pengiktirafan terhadap kecemerlangan dalam bidang penulisan, akademik serta pemartabatan bahasa dan sastera Melayu kepada pelajar institusi pengajian tinggi menerusi Anugerah Bitara DBP mulai tahun ini.

Beliau turut menegaskan kepentingan memelihara tulisan Jawi sebagai khazanah persuratan Melayu yang merakam perkembangan ilmu, pemikiran dan budaya masyarakat, dengan usaha itu perlu digerakkan secara bersama oleh sekolah, ibu bapa, institusi pendidikan dan DBP.

Bagi memperkukuh usaha pemartabatan bahasa kebangsaan, Fadhlina mengumumkan KPM bersetuju menyediakan peruntukan RM10,000 kepada setiap agensi, institusi pengajian tinggi (IPT), Institut Pendidikan Guru (IPG) dan pertubuhan bukan kerajaan (NGO) yang melaksanakan program pemartabatan bahasa kebangsaan pada 2027.

Beliau berkata inisiatif itu bertujuan memperluas penyertaan pelbagai pihak, memperkukuh kerjasama strategik dan menggalakkan pelaksanaan program yang berimpak tinggi sekali gus diharap dapat membina gerakan lebih tersusun dalam usaha memperkukuh penggunaan bahasa kebangsaan di seluruh negara.

Mengenai sambutan Bulan Bahasa Kebangsaan 2026, Fadhlina berkata tema “Bahasa Kita Wajah Kita” mengingatkan bahawa bahasa bukan sekadar alat komunikasi, malah mencerminkan identiti, nilai dan budaya sekali gus menjadi antara asas penting dalam membina persefahaman dan perpaduan dalam masyarakat berbilang kaum dan bahasa ibunda.
Pada majlis tersebut, Bernama Radio menerima Hadiah Citra Sahabat DBP 2026 sebagai pengiktirafan atas sumbangan dan komitemen dalam usaha memperkasakan bahasa Melayu.

Terdahulu, penganjuran berkonsepkan karnival di Padang Kota Lama itu menyediakan ruang penglibatan yang lebih luas kepada masyarakat menerusi pelbagai aktiviti bahasa, sastera, ilmu, seni, budaya dan komuniti.
8a60cdc197d5f2a6: KUALA LUMPUR: A two-goal deficit against Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) usually signals the end of the road for most opponents, but Brunei DPMM head coach Jamie McAllister insists the Southern Tigers were rattled during their 2-0 FA Cup semi-final first-leg clash at the Hassanal Bolkiah National Stadium.

Speaking after the loss on Friday, McAllister praised his side for going toe-to-toe with the reigning champions, arguing that DPMM created enough openings to flip the script and forced JDT into a half-time tactical reshuffle.
"How do I feel about the team? I'm very proud of the players and the performance they put in," McAllister said.

"I thought we matched a very good team and restricted them to very few chances. We had five or six really good chances ourselves, the Welsh header, Jordan (Murray) in the first half, Jordan's header, and two at the end."
The intense competition also spilled over into the technical areas, with McAllister revealing he exchanged words with the JDT bench after they vociferously appealed for a penalty.
"They were screaming for a handball," he said.
"I mean, come on, let the referee do his job. Sit down, you're on the bench, just relax. But that's emotion in the game. That's football, isn't it? It's all about emotion."
However, the JDT camp offered an entirely different perspective, demonstrating the mindset that separates the champions from the rest of the region.
When asked if taking a 2-0 away cushion back to Iskandar Puteri was comfortable enough to seal their passage to the final, JDT head coach Xisco Munoz laughed off the suggestion.
"Never is enough if you are in JDT!" Munoz said.

"Tonight was a positive night for us. An important clean sheet, because it is always important when we are playing (Asian) Champions League Elite games. We need to have the balance in offensive and defensive phases, and the team was in a good way tonight."
JDT took the lead through Bergson da Silva in the 21st minute before Eddy Israfilov doubled their advantage in the 72nd, giving the visitors a 2-0 win and a valuable cushion ahead of the second leg.
c8ebb97105f0d4d1: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Federal narcotics investigators are working in close concert with Indonesian law enforcement to determine whether a Malaysian drug syndicate orchestrated the trafficking of 1.16 tonnes of ketamine hydrochloride aboard a coastal tanker intercepted off North Sumatra.

The 57-metre Mongolian-flagged vessel, MT Global 168, was intercepted off Tanjung Balai Asahan on October 20 after Indonesian authorities linked its registered ownership to Johor-based firm Makmur Marine Petroleum.

A boarding search uncovered 58 sacks concealing 1,160 individually wrapped bricks of high-grade ketamine hydrochloride, with an estimated black-market street value of 3.48 trillion rupiah, or roughly RM800 million.

Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan confirmed that Malaysian police were formally notified of the massive maritime interdiction by Indonesian counterparts yesterday, NST reported.
“NCID will remain in close contact with the Indonesian National Police to obtain further details of the case and exchange relevant intelligence.
“We will also seek information to determine whether any members of drug syndicates operating in Malaysia were involved,” he said.
Preliminary tracking data shared by Indonesian maritime agencies reveals that the tanker embarked from a docking yard in Pasir Gudang, Johor, before stopping to take on bunker fuel at Port Klang.
The vessel then plotted a course towards the open waters of the Andaman Sea, where regional surveillance units flagged anomalous navigation routes between October 14 and 18.
“The vessel was believed to have switched off its Automatic Identification System (AIS) for three days in an attempt to evade detection,” he said.

Hussein added that coastal radar picked up suspicious circular holding patterns off the western coast of Thailand immediately before the tanker turned back toward the Malacca Strait and Sumatran territorial waters.

Indonesian security personnel detained all eight crew members aboard the vessel, comprising seven Indonesian nationals aged between 25 and 71 and a 42-year-old Chinese national. All eight have been designated as formal criminal suspects.
cb8cceb03b0c9a8d: BERLIN, Oct 24 — German police said Saturday they had detained a suspect following a fire at Adolf Hitler’s mountain retreat, known as the Eagle’s Nest, in the state of Bavaria.
“A suspicious person was taken into temporary custody,” police said, following an earlier statement which said firefighters had found the building “completely ablaze”.
The site once housed the Nazi leader’s heavily fortified country residence where he relaxed with his companion Eva Braun and wrote part of his book Mein Kampf.
Emergency services arrived on site at 9:52 pm (1952 GMT) on Friday and found a large fire, the Upper Bavaria South police headquarters said.
Police spokeswoman Lisa Maier said firefighters were struggling to extinguish the blaze due to its remote location, at an altitude of 1,834 metres (6,000 feet).
“The criminal police investigation is ongoing,” she said. — AFP
a234d3c4e8d43681: KUALA LUMPUR: National squash player S Sivasangari moved within one win of clinching the Silicon Valley Open 2026 title after reaching the final in Redwood City, California, on Friday.
The tournament third seed fought back from a game down to defeat India’s Anahat Singh 5-11, 11-6, 11-4, 11-7 in 37 minutes in a rematch of the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games final.
Sivasangari, who retained the women’s singles gold medal at the Asian Games in Japan last month, will face Egypt’s Farida Mohamed in the final later today.
Farida, who is ranked world No 20, made it to the final after defeating American Marina Stefanoni 11-3, 4-11, 11-6, 6-11, 11-8.

The victory put Sivasangari, who is world No 4, through to her second consecutive final at the tournament, giving her a chance to make amends for last year’s 10-12, 11-4, 4-11, 4-11 defeat to American Olivia Weaver.
9ddb22916fcb5544: KAJANG: The family of Noorizwan Zulkefly, 42, who died while in police custody at Cheras district police headquarters, has sought the help of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar for a transparent investigation into his death.
The family turned up at Anwar's residence in Bandar Sungai Long this morning to hand over a memorandum to the prime minister's representative.
The family accompanied by their lawyers gathered at the guardhouse before being allowed into the compound.

The memorandum, submitted by Noorizwan's younger brother Nooranis Zulkeﬂy and lawyers from Lawyers for Liberty (LFL), said the family had serious concerns over the injuries found on the deceased's body during the post-mortem.
The family is now seeking immediate action and a transparent investigation into his death.
A post-mortem at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) revealed no damage to his internal organs but confirmed multiple external bodily injuries, police said.
The cause of death remains undetermined and has been classified as "pending laboratory analysis" while pathologists await toxicology and histology findings from the Chemistry Department.
Noorizwan was detained by police on Sept 19 by Cheras police for suspected drug possession and theft/housebreaking offences.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus had said that Noorizwan had been managed in strict compliance with standard operating procedures before suddenly falling ill.
After 11 days in detention, he was transferred to HCTM on Sept 30 for emergency treatment and was pronounced dead early on Oct 1.

Fadil also highlighted that the deceased carried 44 prior criminal records, consisting of 18 narcotics infractions and 26 other offences, and had allegedly admitted to 17 unsolved break-ins across Cheras.
Bukit Aman's Criminal Investigation and Deaths in Custody Unit (USJKT) is leading the inquiry and to date have interviewed 78 individuals.
46ebc40d302573b8: BARCELONA, Oct 24 — Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho will renew one of football’s most bitter rivalries on Sunday when he takes charge of his first Clasico since returning to the club, with La Liga leaders Barcelona awaiting him at Camp Nou.

The Portuguese veteran’s first spell at Madrid was defined in large part by his battle to end Barca’s dominance under Pep Guardiola, with relations between the Spanish giants slumping to their lowest ebb.
Mourinho managed to break Barca’s spell by guiding Real Madrid to the Spanish title in 2012, the crowning achievement of his reign from 2010-13.

Clasicos became increasingly compelling during that period, some would say not for the right reasons, as he and his staff clashed with their Barcelona counterparts both pitch-side and verbally in the media.
The 63-year-old worked as an assistant at Barca under Bobby Robson and Louis van Gaal in the 1990s but was overlooked for Guardiola in 2008 when the Catalans replaced Frank Rijkaard.
Mourinho’s frequent battles with Guardiola, Lionel Messi and even with Madrid’s own icons like Iker Casillas sometimes overshadowed his sporting achievements.
The most infamous flashpoint was when Mourinho poked then Barca assistant coach Tito Vilanova in the eye in August 2011.
Earlier that year, at the end of the prior season, Madrid and Barca clashed four times in just 18 days, illustrating the intensity of the rivalry.
The first was in La Liga, a 1-1 draw, which helped Barcelona take a step towards retaining the Spanish title as Madrid trailed them.
Mourinho’s Madrid beat Barca to win the Copa del Rey in the second, with Cristiano Ronaldo scoring the winner in extra-time.

Then the Catalans got the better of Los Blancos in a Champions League semi-final double header, winning the first leg 2-0 in the Santiago Bernabeu, with Madrid defender Pepe sent off. Mourinho called it a “scandal”.
Barcelona held Real Madrid to a 1-1 draw in the second leg to reach the final, which they went on to win.
It was in this period that Guardiola said he could not and would not compete with the “boss” Mourinho in the press room.
Stopping Flick’s Barca
Mourinho has hit the ground running in his second spell at Madrid in that regard.

The coach brandished print-outs of incidents after losing the derby clash to try and prove his point that Atletico Madrid deserved two red cards, and refused to attend a press conference after Vinicius Junior was sent off against Villarreal.
Many believe Mourinho employs these tactics as a distraction to take the pressure off his team when they are not performing.

A victory in the Clasico might encourage him to focus on the football, and stopping Hansi Flick’s side – back-to-back Spanish champions – is one of the main reasons he was rehired by president Florentino Perez.
Flick’s Barca have won six of seven Clasicos against Real Madrid since the German arrived, scoring 22 goals and shipping only 11.
Mourinho insists it is impossible for his team to be at the level he wants them to be at after such a short time in charge.
“I’ve been here for over a hundred days. Obviously, we are not where I want, but there are things we are doing better today than before,” said the coach.
Madrid have won their last four matches between La Liga and the Champions League, and after sharing minutes around early in the season, some preferences are emerging.

Although Mourinho said initially he did not see midfielder Federico Valverde as a right-back, where he has been used in the past, he has selected the Uruguayan there in the last two games, ahead of Denzel Dumfries and Trent Alexander-Arnold.
“We created a lot on that side, and Fede had a fantastic match,” said Mourinho after the Leipzig win.

In Valverde’s place in midfield Mourinho deployed Arda Guler against Sevilla on Sunday and then Bernardo Silva against the German side, with Madrid improving on the ball and retaining more possession.
However the Clasico poses a different challenge. Mourinho, who deployed defender Pepe in midfield against Barca, may revert to type to try and spoil the hosts’ flowing football. — AFP

59f95d95e40ccc22: PHILLIP ISLAND: Marc Marquez stormed home first from pole in the Australian MotoGP sprint race on Saturday to seize control of the world championship from Jorge Martin who crashed out challenging him for the lead.
The reigning seven-time world champion, who dominated qualifying, had too much power in his Ducati to surge to the chequered flag ahead of his brother Alex in the 13-lap contest.
Victory put him 10 points clear of fellow Spaniard Martin in the standings ahead of the final MotoGP ever around the waterfront Phillip Island circuit on Sunday.
Martin, who started from fourth under dark clouds but with the rain staying away, took the lead on lap three in a ding-dong battle with his rival.
But he lost control on lap eight while challenging for the lead once again to put a massive dent in his championship ambitions.
"It was a tight battle," said Marquez. "Of course, I gave everything. I was aggressive, and he (Martin) was faster than me.
"But just I tried to defend in the best way possible. Both of us we are riding to the limit. Both of us, we deserve the victory because we are pushing a lot.
"But, you know, racing is like it is."
His brother Alex, who started second, filled an all-Ducati podium with Fabio Di Giannantonio.
Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi, who won the MotoGP last week in Indonesia, was fourth to remain third in the standings, 50 points behind Marquez.
Pedro Acosta (KTM) came fifth and Ai Ogura (Aprilia) sixth.
Marc Marquez held the line to be first at the opening corner with Martin up to second with Johann Zarco third and it stayed that way at the end of lap one.
Martin was pressing hard and he took the lead on lap three as the race became a dogfight between the two championship leaders as they pulled clear of the field.
A big mistake from Martin running wide on lap five opened the door again for Marquez, with the lead changing hands several times as they battled for supremacy.
But Martin pushed too much and sensationally lost control on lap eight, skidding out to end his race.
Phillip Island has been a staple on the calendar since 1997 but the Australian race is moving next year to a street circuit in Adelaide.
d140772af07dc39b: KUANTAN: The welfare and well-being of teachers must never be taken lightly, Prime Minister's Political Secretary Datuk Ahmad Farhan Fauzi said.
He said teachers are among the noblest members of society, not merely imparting knowledge but also shaping character, thinking, and a nation's fundamental values.

"We often speak of the immense role teachers play in shaping children's futures. However, while placing high expectations on educators, we must never forget that they, too, have lives, families, responsibilities and aspirations of their own," he said at the Kuantan District Education Office's 2025 Excellent Service Awards ceremony here today, where 642 people were recognised for their service.

Farhan said education remained a key priority for the Madani government and continued to receive attention, including through an increased allocation of nearly RM69 billion for the Education Ministry under the 2027 Budget.
He said the welfare of specific groups of educators was also being prioritised, including through an increase in the Special Needs Education Teaching Incentive from RM250 to RM300 per month.
Farhan also announced a contribution of RM30,000 as a commitment to supporting educators' welfare and educational excellence in the district.

"I hope this contribution will be used prudently to meet the district's educational needs, particularly to improve facilities, strengthen teaching and learning, and create a more conducive educational environment.
"Hopefully, the benefits will be felt directly by teachers and pupils, contributing to improvements in the quality and performance of local education," he said.
4f3f034c8f9c186c: BERLIN: German police said Saturday they had detained a suspect following a fire at Adolf Hitler's mountain retreat, known as the Eagle's Nest, in the state of Bavaria.
"A suspicious person was taken into temporary custody," police said, following an earlier statement which said firefighters had found the building "completely ablaze."

73361b85eaa21cc5: PHILLIP ISLAND (Australia), Oct 24 — World champion Marc Marquez beat brother Alex to clinch pole position Saturday at the Australian MotoGP, but he needed some white-knuckle laps to do so after crashing early on.
Under dark clouds and with spots of rain falling, the Spanish Ducati rider powered round the waterfront circuit at Phillip Island with a blistering lap of 1min 34.203 sec.
It was enough to topple Alex, also on a Ducati, by a massive 1.494sec, with Honda’s Johann Zarco third to join them on the front row.
Championship leader Jorge Martin, who is two points clear of Marc Marquez with five rounds of the season left, was fourth, but well off the pace.
Home hero Jack Miller and last year’s winner Raul Fernandez accompany him on the second row.
Marco Bezzecchi, who won last week in Indonesia and is third in the standings, 46 points behind Martin, will start in ninth.
“You cannot crash in the first lap because it means that you don’t have a lap time. So it was a big mistake,” said Marc Marquez.
“But the team was ready with the other bike, I kept focus and that last lap was a good lap.”
Marquez, who dominated morning practice, slid off on his first flying lap at Turn 4 as he pushed too hard.
Undeterred, he limped back to the pits and climbed onto his spare bike and immediately set the new fastest time.
It was surpassed by Zarco, but Marquez came back out at the death to blitz a new quickest time and secure his 78th career pole.
The sprint race is later Saturday and the main event on Sunday, with thunderstorms forecast.
They will go ahead without Honda’s Luca Marini, who has a virus and will take no further part in the weekend action.
Phillip Island has been a staple on the calendar since 1997 but the Australian race is moving next year to a street circuit in Adelaide. — AFP
e0787d74eaecf26f: The prime minister has defined and dominated his country’s politics for three decades and is putting his rivals on the defensive before Tuesday’s general election They chant his name, they cheer and clap – and yet he is not the most dominant person in the room. Looming over the crowd that has gathered to hear Gadi Eisenkot, the former general who is the lead opposition challenger in Tuesday’s Israeli election, is a man who is not there. It is the man Eisenkot seeks to replace as prime minister, the man who first served in that role three decades ago and who has held it, on and off, for 19 of the past 30 years. It is Benjamin Netanyahu. Naturally, the warm-up speakers at this evening rally in the modest city of Modi’in, halfway between Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, stress the virtues of Eisenkot, a son of working-class Moroccan Jews who rose through the ranks to become chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces and entered politics only four years ago. But every sentence might as well end with two words that go unspoken: unlike Bibi. Continue reading...
58337fdb26412cc0: Chancellor says government to commit hundreds of millions to develop ‘distinctively British’ approach to AI John Healey has pledged to use Wednesday’s budget to harness the power of artificial intelligence to bolster Britain’s security and prosperity against the risks in the accelerating global technology arms race. As he prepares for his debut budget, the chancellor said that Andy Burnham’s government would commit hundreds of millions of pounds to develop a “distinctively British” approach to AI that would capitalise on the benefits of the frontier technology. 3cf7348afefcb607: We’ve heard much about the end of the west. c87c1ff0b3a40ff1: PALANGKARAYA: Hundreds of students protested late Friday in Indonesia's Palangkaraya, demanding the government do more to tackle a wildfire crisis that has shrouded their city and the wider region in toxic haze for months.

The students, many wearing surgical masks, gathered under an eerily orange sky with severely reduced visibility and waved banners urging authorities to declare a national emergency to free up more aid.

"The officials are morons, yet they get fantastic perks while the lives of the common people are tragic," read one protest placard nailed to a wall outside the office of the governor of Central Kalimantan -- an Indonesian province on the island of Borneo where the fires are taking place.
The demonstrators sang the Indonesia Pusaka patriotic song and engaged in light skirmishes with police.
No injuries or arrests were reported and as night fell, the protesters cleared up their trash before dispersing peacefully.

"We call upon the Central Kalimantan provincial government to state clearly that it is unable to mitigate this disaster, so that the situation may be officially designated a national disaster," protest leader Yuyun Sanjaya told the crowd.
"How is it possible that such thick, dense smoke is being inhaled by helpless elderly people and newborn infants, and the government simply lets it happen?"
Wildfires have burned more than 1.9 million hectares in the nine months to September, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas -- a figure the government has not confirmed or denied.
The resulting haze has sickened hundreds of thousands in Indonesia and reached as far as Malaysia, Singapore and East Timor.
Amid diplomatic objections from neighbouring countries, patience has also been running thin at home, with sporadic anti-government protests.
On Thursday, Indonesian school children prayed for rain on Java island, where fires have also ravaged several regencies and conservation areas.
c96e06453ab824d4: LONDON, Oct 24 — Prince William has made a rare royal appearance on a BBC chat show, with the heir to the throne confessing he would have liked to join the police or be a DJ.
The Prince of Wales appeared on an episode set to air yesterday evening, to promote his Earthshot Prize, which goes to environmental causes.
The show’s host, comedian Graham Norton, is known for his A-list guests and mildly ribbing celebrities.

Wearing a blue suit, shirt and tie, William was roaring with laughter in images released ahead of the show on his and his wife’s Instagram. He sat on the show’s sofa next to actresses Cate Blanchett and Hannah Waddingham and conservationist Robert Irwin, all involved in the prize.

Hello! magazine wrote that William is the first working royal to appear on a British talk show although Sarah Ferguson, the former wife of William’s uncle, the former prince Andrew, was interviewed by Norton when she still had a royal title.
The Graham Norton Show is now in its 33rd series and is the broadcaster’s most watched chat show. Recent guests include Madonna.
The BBC reported there were “cheers and gasps from the audience” when William appeared as a surprise guest.
He will present the Earthshot Prize in Mumbai on November 17. Launched in 2020, the prize supports initiatives that help tackle environmental crises such as climate change.
As with previous competitions, this year’s winners will receive £1 million (RM5.3 million) each “to accelerate the impact of their innovative solutions”, organisers said.

William was asked whether he ever fantasised about another job rather than becoming king, telling Norton: “I did want to be a policeman when I was younger. I thought I could make a good one,” adding that he also went through “a phase of wanting to be a DJ — I wasn’t very good.”

William spoke of his family’s love for The Celebrity Traitors, a devious reality show currently topping ratings. He also said he was a “big fan” of director Christopher Nolan’s Dark Knight trilogy about Batman, which he called “psychologically dark and deep”.

The prince has kept tight-lipped about the return to Britain of his estranged brother Prince Harry, who said in an interview this week with GQ magazine that he wanted things to “work out” with his father, King Charles III, and William, his elder brother. — AFP
f33a11f68dd055df: WASHINGTON, Oct 24 — The US Department of Defense has designated Confucius Institutes, Chinese-funded cultural centres on American university campuses, a threat to US national security, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Friday.
Washington considers the centres to be propaganda tools of the Chinese Communist Party, and has taken steps to shut them down.
Hegseth said the Defense Department took action after such organisations had reappeared in disguised forms.
“We added these sleeper organisations to our list of institutions that threaten our national security,” Hegseth said in a video.

“It turns out that 80 new propaganda cells across 30 universities had popped up using different names and different charters, but with the same mission: to steal intellectual property and to infiltrate the minds of American students,” he continued.
Hegseth said that the Department of Defense had dismantled all the centres within the last two months. — AFP
2e66dde732060e52: KUALA LUMPUR: Dua rakyat Malaysia yang cedera ringan sedang dirawat di Taiwan akibat kesan Taufan Champi, menurut Kementerian Luar.
Kementerian Luar yang turut dikenali Wisma Putra memaklumkan perkara itu disahkan Pusat Persahabatan dan Perdagangan Malaysia di Taipei yang menyediakan bantuan konsular kepada dua mangsa terbabit.

"(Pusat) berkenaan terus berhubung rapat dengan kumpulan pelajar Malaysia dan pihak berkuasa tempatan untuk memantau perkembangan dan menjaga kebajikan rakyat Malaysia di Taiwan," katanya dalam kenyataan.

Rakyat Malaysia yang memerlukan bantuan konsular atau mempunyai maklumat warga Malaysia yang mungkin memerlukan bantuan di kawasan terjejas, digesa menghubungi Pusat Persahabatan dan Perdagangan Malaysia di Taipei menerusi talian +886 972 349 343 atau e-mel mwtaipei@kln.gov.my.
Wisma Putra berkata, pihaknya memantau keadaan dengan teliti susulan impak taufan itu, yang membawa angin kencang, hujan lebat dan gangguan meluas terhadap pengangkutan serta perkhidmatan awam.
Taufan Champi mengakibatkan pembatalan penerbangan dan gangguan perkhidmatan feri, dengan keadaan cuaca buruk dijangka berterusan di beberapa bahagian Taiwan.
Menurut kementerian, pihak berkuasa tempatan telah memindahkan penduduk dari kawasan banjir dan tanah runtuh, termasuk kawasan berhampiran empangan yang dilanda tanah runtuh di Daerah Hualien.

"Rakyat Malaysia yang menetap atau melawat Taiwan dinasihatkan sentiasa berwaspada, mengelakkan kawasan pantai dan pergunungan, selain mematuhi semua arahan keselamatan dan pemindahan yang dikeluarkan pihak berkuasa tempatan."
Rakyat Malaysia juga digalakkan memantau nasihat cuaca tempatan dan mengelakkan perjalanan tidak perlu ke kawasan terjejas banjir, tanah runtuh atau bahaya berkaitan cuaca lain.

Wisma Putra berkata, memandangkan gangguan pengangkutan berterusan, rakyat Malaysia yang mempunyai rancangan perjalanan dinasihatkan menyemak status penerbangan atau feri secara langsung dengan pengendali sebelum ke lapangan terbang atau terminal.

Kementerian menggalakkan semua rakyat Malaysia mendaftar dan sentiasa mengemas kini butiran perhubungan mereka menerusi portal e-Konsular di https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my bagi memudahkan komunikasi dan akses bantuan konsular tepat pada masanya.
c82824b0de0945c6: BUDAPEST: Hungarian prime minister Peter Magyar said Friday that the country was striving to be a reliable EU partner, as he sought to rebuild trust with allies after Viktor Orban's 16-year rule.

His speech, given on the national day commemorating the 70th anniversary of the 1956 anti-Soviet uprising, which was brutally crushed by Moscow with tanks, was in stark contrast to Kremlin-friendly nationalist Orban, who frequently used such addresses to attack Brussels and compare the EU to the Soviet Union.

"Hungary is not a 'ferry country', it cannot drift endlessly between East and West. In 1956, the Hungarian people made a clear choice: we belong to a free, democratic Europe," Magyar told a crowd in front of the parliament waving a sea of national flags.
"We want to be reliable allies who sit at the shared table with our heads held high, not fortune-seekers who isolate themselves through blackmail and pursuing a separate path," he added.
Hungary hosted EU leaders, prime ministers and other foreign dignitaries from over 40 countries for the commemoration.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen addressed a ceremonial session of the parliament boycotted by the opposition, including Orban's Fidesz party.
In the crowd outside, Magyar's supporters said they felt the pro-EU turn was long overdue.

"Hungary never turned its back on the EU -- it was our (previous) government that did. We have finally regained our country, so that our room for manoeuvre remains within the right parameters, just as we had hoped it would be," Attila Rothi, a 56-year-old stock trader, told AFP.

"We belong there, and so we must find our place within that community, even if that involves offering criticism (of the EU). And I believe Magyar is doing just that," said Veronika, 68, a retiree, who refused to give her last name.
She cited as examples financing for Ukraine and migration policy, where Magyar is seen following his predecessor's hardline policies.
"But let us be constructive, and not hostile," she added.
84841100ae7e6825: PARIS, Oct 24 — France will deploy about 70,000 police nationwide as it braces for new protests on Saturday after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago.
Protests by high school students over learning conditions sparked a movement that has since spread nationwide, fuelled by broader anger over the rising cost of living.

About 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said at a news conference in Paris, warning that calls for violence and looting were circulating on social media.

The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen as the frontrunner and indicating her position has been strengthened by the latest events.

Adding to tensions, Le Pen is due at the weekend to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected and local authorities fearing clashes as counter-protesters also head to the city south of Paris.

Macron met representatives of secondary school pupils on Friday, but they emerged from the talks urging students to keep protesting until the government put forward concrete proposals to address their demands.
Offenders jailed
Macron’s government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations last Saturday.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
French President Emmanuel Macron speaks with community members at the town hall in Trappes, near Paris, on October 23, 2026. — AFP pic
Courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said.
On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, accusing “ultra-left” groups of having sought to “bring down the republic” last weekend.
An extreme-left group in western France posted on its website a call for its supporters to be “uncatchable, unpredictable, to evade the deployment” of police.
Protest restrictions
Authorities have stepped up security measures and imposed restrictions on protests.
In Orleans, between 20,000 and 30,000 people are expected to come out against Le Pen’s National Rally party, but the gathering will be barred from the city centre, the prefecture said.
In the southeastern city of Lyon, central areas will also be off-limits to demonstrators this weekend.
In Paris, police overturned a previous permit for union-led protesters to march between Bastille and Nation squares in the east.
The force said the parade could instead go in the afternoon along an alternative route on the southeastern edge of the city.
Unions vowed to push ahead on the banned route, citing safety concerns over the alternative.

Authorities in Marseille had also banned protests but announced Friday that a union-organised demonstration would be allowed on an “exceptional basis” — the only one authorised in the southern Bouches-du-Rhone department.
In the capital, leading museums including the Louvre will be closed on Saturday while the Art Basel art fair is being cut short.
Police ‘responsibility’
The restrictions, including outright bans on protests in some cities, have drawn criticism.
Amnesty International denounced what it called “a slide toward authoritarian practice”, saying the measures were “jeopardising the right to demonstrate peacefully”.
About 20 per cent more members of the security forces will be deployed this weekend following questions over police preparedness and intelligence gathering ahead of last week’s violence.

“Police have a responsibility both to ensure that protests can take place peacefully and safely and to protect the public from violent disorder,” said Eva Cosse, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch.
She voiced alarm over reports of children being severely injured by crowd-control weapons during recent gatherings.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

French far-right Rassemblement National MP Marine Le Pen speaks during a session at the National Assembly in Paris on October 20, 2026, ahead of her party’s congress in Orleans this weekend. — AFP pic
The violence has tarnished the image of France ahead of elections that could be a turning point in its modern history, with the government’s debt pile also troubling investors.
A new poll by Harris Interactive for M6/RTL made after the violence showed Le Pen soaring ahead on 33-35 per cent in the first round of voting for the presidential elections.
It predicted that hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon was on course to face her in the run-off where Le Pen would emerge as an easy winner on about 70 per cent of the vote. — AFP
a3e6d7159ab873f4: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has sounded a midday thunderstorm advisory for multiple states across Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak, warning of torrential rain, lightning, and gusty winds until 2.00pm today.

cross East Malaysia, Sarawak accounts for the widest geographic coverage under the current bulletin. 5d98a3b087d77640: LOS ANGELES, Oct 24 — Ryan Gosling’s indie-rock band Dead Man’s Bones is set to release new music, 17 years after the duo’s only album, German Press Agency (dpa) reported.
