e217f4452da7d871: BEIJING: Moonshot AI has reduced the cyber-offensive capabilities of its newest model, the Chinese startup said on Saturday, as fears grow that increasingly autonomous AI could turbocharge hacking.

Beijing-based Moonshot announced the curbs while introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, which it describes as its most capable 3-trillion-parameter-class open-weight model. The company plans to publish the model's weights -- files allowing outside developers to run and modify it on their own systems -- by Nov 4.
Moonshot said it removed cyber-related data from the training corpus and reinforcement-learning environments used to develop the model, while retaining general coding skills.
"We aim not to release open weights that would extend the absolute frontier of cyber capability," the company said.

Governments, technology companies and security researchers are growing increasingly concerned that AI could make sophisticated hacking easier and cheaper. Models that can write code, operate software tools and complete long, multi-step tasks may help users identify weaknesses in programs and automate parts of cyberattacks.

China proposed export controls last week that would ban exports of AI-driven malware-generation and mutation technology and restrict AI-assisted vulnerability-discovery tools. The draft measures, which remain open for public comment, cite the risk that such capabilities could be used against critical infrastructure, defence-industrial and core government systems, or to bypass security protections.
Moonshot said open-weight models can improve security by helping more organisations inspect and secure their own software, including older systems that receive little attention.

Unlike proprietary, closed-weight AI systems, however, open-weight releases make central oversight more difficult. Once the files are widely distributed, the original developer has less ability to restrict access, monitor use or update safeguards than with a hosted service.

K3.1 Pro scored 81.0% on its internal cyber benchmark, compared with 90.5% for a similar version without the risk-reduction measures, the company said. The test involved finding and exploiting software vulnerabilities in a controlled environment. Moonshot said the comparison showed that filtering cyber-related data reduced the model's offensive cyber performance, although it still outperformed its predecessor. The results have not been independently verified.

K3.1 Pro has a 1-million-token context window, allowing it to process very large amounts of text at once. Moonshot also released a faster version, K3.1 Pro Highspeed, which it said runs at two to three times the speed of the standard model.
2a8456a4aeeb8e78: TAIPEI, Oct 24 — Emergency crews scrambled on Saturday to restore power to tens of thousands of households in Taiwan after Typhoon Champi’s fierce winds battered the island as the storm moves towards China and Japan.
More than 5,000 people were evacuated from their homes ahead of the storm, which toppled trees, brought down power lines, and triggered brief flooding.
One person was killed and over 500 injured since Thursday when the government began issuing warnings about the approaching typhoon.
Around 56,000 households are still without power as Champi continues to buffet the island, with nearly 24 centimetres (9.4 inches) of rain recorded in the western county of Miaoli on Saturday.
Most shops across northern and central Taiwan were closed for a second day as the typhoon gradually moves away from the island’s northeast and heads north towards China and Japan.

“Although the period of the typhoon’s most severe impact has passed, we would like to remind everyone that winds and waves in the waters around Taiwan remain strong as the typhoon moves northwards,” the Central Weather Administration’s Wuu Woan-hwa said at a briefing.
Champi is the latest in a busy Pacific storm season turbocharged by the El Nino weather phenomenon that has caused unprecedented warming in the equatorial Pacific.
The storm was briefly a super typhoon as it crossed the ocean in recent days, with reported maximum sustained wind speeds of nearly 300 kilometres (186 miles) per hour.
It was packing wind speeds of 176 kph on Saturday, according to the latest update from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center.
The storm’s intensity weakened overnight as it made a loop off Taiwan’s northeastern county of Yilan, where it dumped 65 cm of rain since Thursday, the forecaster said.
Martha Wang said she was afraid of being “blown away” by the wind as she rode her scooter across a bridge in New Taipei City on Saturday morning.
“I was really scared because I was on the bridge. My scooter was shaking,” the 55-year-old secretary told AFP.
William Yu, however, was unfazed by the storm, saying it “wasn’t any stronger than other typhoons.”
“I went to the convenience store to eat yesterday (evening) and everything was fine,” the 55-year-old librarian said.
‘Strong winds and heavy rain’
Authorities in China warned of “strong winds and heavy rain” as Champi approaches the country’s east coast, the state-controlled broadcaster said.
Some train services have been suspended and tens of thousands evacuated from their homes in Shanghai.
“Some areas of Jiangsu, Shanghai, Zhejiang, and other regions are expected to experience heavy to torrential rainfall,” it said.
Dozens of flights have been cancelled in the region, including in Japan’s southernmost prefecture of Okinawa where the government said two people were injured in the typhoon.
The United Nations said Wednesday that the El Nino system gripping the planet is heading off the charts and that countries should take urgent action to prepare for the worst.
El Nino is expected to peak in December, but the human impact is set to last into 2027 and beyond.

The warming phase of a natural climate cycle, El Nino temporarily raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather that can increase the risk of drought and flooding and exacerbate human-caused global warming. — AFP
dd4e86e643c2d420: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Two Malaysian nationals are currently receiving medical treatment for minor injuries in the aftermath of Typhoon Champi on Taiwan, the Foreign Ministry said.

The ministry which is also known as Wisma Putra said the matter was confirmed by the Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre in Taipei, which is also providing the necessary consular assistance to both individuals.

“(The centre) remains in close communication with Malaysian student groups and the relevant local authorities to monitor developments and safeguard the welfare of Malaysians in Taiwan,” the ministry said in a statement on Saturday.

Malaysians requiring consular assistance, or those with information concerning other Malaysian nationals who may require assistance in the affected areas, are urged to contact the Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre in Taipei at +886 972 349 343 or via email at mwtaipei@kln.gov.my.
Wisma Putra said it is closely monitoring the typhoon situation, which has brought strong winds and heavy rainfall. Adverse weather conditions are expected to persist in parts of Taiwan.

The typhoon has caused widespread flight cancellations and disruptions to ferry services. In light of this, Malaysians with upcoming travel plans are advised to check their flight or ferry status directly with the respective operators before proceeding to airports or terminals.

The ministry is advising Malaysians residing in or visiting Taiwan to monitor local weather advisories, avoid coastal and mountainous areas, and adhere to safety instructions and evacuation orders issued by local authorities.

It said local authorities have already evacuated residents from flood- and landslide-prone areas, including areas near a landslide dam in Hualien County. Malaysians are told to avoid unnecessary travel to such areas.

Wisma Putra is also encouraging all Malaysians to register and regularly update their contact details via the e-Konsular portal at https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my to facilitate timely communication and access to consular assistance.

e001ce55820ff54a: SYDNEY: A tsunami warning has been lifted after a magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck off the coast of Vanuatu on Saturday, the Pacific Tsunami Warning Centre said.
The earthquake's magnitude was revised to 6.9, down from an earlier estimate of 7.2, the centre said in an update.
Vanuatu's Geological Hazards Department had earlier issued a warning urging people in coastal areas to evacuate to higher ground.
The quake's epicentre was about 200km north-west of Port-Olry on the island of Santo, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS), which also reported a second nearby quake of magnitude 6.3.

Vanuatu's former prime minister Alatoi Ishmael Kalsakau wrote on Facebook that aftershocks were continuing. He counted five quakes on Saturday and urged residents to "be safe" and check apps regularly.
Earthquakes are common in Vanuatu, a low-lying archipelago that straddles the tectonic Ring of Fire, an arc of seismic activity stretching through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin.
9858eb93132e75ea: RIYADH, Oct 24 — The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said on Saturday it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh by the Iran-backed group.
Two explosions rang out in Riyadh early Saturday, an AFP journalist in the Saudi capital said, as the Houthis keep up strikes on the kingdom.
An early warning system was activated to alert residents to a potential threat, the Saudi civil defence said.
“Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthi terrorist militia toward Riyadh,” coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki posted on X.
A drone was also intercepted in the country’s Eastern Province, al-Malki said in an earlier post on Saturday.
Saudi Arabia has come under sustained attack from the Iran-backed group this month, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the country’s deadliest in years.
Tehran has denied having anything to do with attacks by the Houthis after Saudi Arabia accused Iran of having encouraged the group’s escalation against the kingdom.
Following an uneasy four-year truce, fighting reignited in Yemen in July, months into the US-Iran conflict that has plunged the wider region into crisis.
The Yemen conflict has killed hundreds of thousands of people in one of the world’s poorest countries, which was already suffering a vast humanitarian crisis. — AFP
8efe4c2deeca5f9f: KUALA LUMPUR: Kim Pan Gon delivered the news every Malaysian football fan was longing to hear, confirming that winger Faisal Halim will return to action in "the next few weeks."
The Selangor head coach, however, could not hide his irritation over a nagging tactical flaw exposed by an injury-ravaged Kuching City side.

Speaking after the Red Giants secured a slender 2–1 win in their FA Cup semi-final first leg at the MBPJ Stadium, Pan Gon was startled when asked whether Faisal would sit out the rest of the calendar year as he continues his recovery from a calf muscle injury sustained during the last international window earlier this month.

"This year? (Faisal to return on the pitch). Oh, definitely this year, okay! I mean, next few weeks, next few weeks. We are waiting for Faisal Halim, but soon he will come. Soon he will come, don't worry," Pan Gon said while expressing how upset he is at losing him.
But any relief surrounding the forward's imminent comeback was swiftly overshadowed by the South Korean's assessment of his team's defensive discipline.

Despite dominating possession and taking a lead into the second leg, Pan Gon was incensed by the manner in which Selangor conceded the opening goal, repeatedly branding their vulnerability on the counter-attack as unacceptable.
"To me, for us, it is a bad habit, a bad habit, a bad habit," Pan Gon said.
"We give away a counter-attack. That, we have to correct. If we want to be a strong team… the last few games we give away counter-attacks.

"We worked to correct it last week, we put some effort into it, but still it happened again. We thought the game had stopped, but mentally we must be very strong. Until the whistle, we must play. That's a bad habit, and we have to correct it."
Pan Gon's frustration was compounded by the fact that it was an injury-hit Kuching that repeatedly sliced open his backline.

Far from arriving at full strength, the Borneo side were missing key striker Ronald Ngah and lost forward Safawi Rasid to a hamstring injury during the contest, leaving head coach Aidil Sharin Sahak forced to assemble a makeshift front line.
"Ronald Ngah is injured for maybe two months, so this is where Plan B came in with Jerome playing as a lone striker today, and we tried Dylan Wenzel in the second half," Aidil said.
"(Joao) Pedro was also 50-50, but he still played and wanted to contribute. Today, the only thing I see is Safawi having a hamstring (injury) as well."
Despite the growing casualty list, Kuching refused to roll over, creating several clear-cut chances that rattled the hosts until the final whistle.
"The boys gave everything tonight," he said.
"We created chances. Jerome one-versus-one, Dylan also, and Gabriel Peres tried to score. We were just unlucky not to get a goal in the last minute."
Selangor took the lead through Ramdhan Saifullah in the ninth minute, but Eduardo Sosa equalised 10 minutes later before completing his brace in the 58th minute to seal a 2-1 first-leg victory.

b7d94478eb6f3d9c: PETALING JAYA: Two Malaysians in Taiwan are receiving treatment for minor injuries following Typhoon Champi's landfall, which left at least one dead and hundreds injured.
The foreign ministry said this was confirmed by the Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre in Taipei City, adding that the pair was receiving consular assistance, Bernama reported.

"The centre continues to be in close contact with Malaysian students in Taiwan and local authorities to monitor developments and preserve the wellbeing of Malaysians there," Wisma Putra said in a statement.
It advised Malaysians living in or visiting Taiwan to exercise caution amid the typhoon, and particularly avoid beaches and mountainous areas.

The typhoon, packing gusts of around 126km per hour near its centre, has led to power cuts and fallen trees in Taiwan. One man on the island of Liuqiu died after being swept away by waves during the typhoon.
It also led to nearly 1,000 flights being cancelled yesterday and 242 today.
0f082e1523bf2fd9: LONDON, Oct 24 — The hunt for the next James Bond will reportedly reach its final stages this weekend as screen tests for the role will be held in London, PA Media/dpa reported.

Callum Turner, star of One Night Only, Jack Lowden of Slow Horses, and Josh O’Connor of The Crown are among those being considered for screen tests, which could begin as early as yesterday, according to Deadline.
‘Slow Horses’ star Jack Lowden has emerged as a possible contender to become the next James Bond. — AFP pic
Contrary to previous rumours, Euphoria actor Jacob Elordi and Sinners star Jack O’Connell are not among those trying out for the role, according to The Hollywood Reporter.
It is said there will be three components to the screen tests: stunts, camera presence, and dialogue.
The actor chosen will replace Daniel Craig, who took over the role of Bond with Casino Royale (2006) and bowed out after his fifth film, No Time To Die (2021).
Amy Pascal, who will produce the next Bond film, told Deadline earlier this year about casting: “I would say (an announcement by) the end of the year is a good bet.
“We are being really, really methodical. Having worked with (producer) Barbara Broccoli at the studio, I mean, Daniel Craig is a hard act to follow.
“And it’s got to be something really different that is stirring, exciting, and different.”
The next Bond film, currently untitled, will be directed by Dune’s Denis Villeneuve and Harry Potter producer David Heyman will work alongside Pascal on the project.
Representatives for Turner, Lowden, O’Connor, and Amazon Studios have been contacted for comment. — Bernama-PA Media/dpa
9f7a0b8b42dd2d4d: KUALA LUMPUR: Components of a counter-unmanned aerial system (C-UAS) supplied by Japan under its Official Security Assistance (OSA) programme will be deployed at several locations, including Sepanggar and Labuan, to strengthen Malaysia's defences against drone attacks.

Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the system was needed amid a changing geopolitical environment and the need to safeguard Malaysia's land and maritime domains, particularly amid overlapping territorial claims and rivalry among major powers in the South China Sea.
"We are facing a different geopolitical situation, and we are in a region with significant challenges.

"As I have often said, we are a maritime nation. We protect our land, but we must also protect our entire maritime domain. We need to safeguard our waters, including the Strait of Malacca and the South China Sea.
"We also know that the South China Sea is an area of overlapping territorial claims. We must ensure that we can maintain control over our maritime domain.

"We also know that the South China Sea is an area of conflict or rivalry among major powers. We must be prepared," he said at a press conference after the opening ceremony of the 100th National General Assembly of the Armed Forces Veterans Association.

Japan will provide Malaysia with a C-UAS system worth about RM40 million under its 2026 OSA programme, following an agreement signed by Khaled and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi during Khaled's recent working visit to Japan.
Khaled said Malaysia and Japan had longstanding bilateral relations, with defence cooperation gaining momentum in recent years following changes in Japan's defence policy.
During the visit, Malaysia urged Tokyo to continue the OSA programme and ensure future assistance was aligned with the country's priority defence needs, particularly maritime security.
"We hope the OSA programme will continue and not be discontinued, as it is helping us develop our capabilities," he said.

Khaled said Malaysia had also requested that future assistance focus on strategic priorities, including strengthening its ability to safeguard its maritime domain amid geopolitical challenges and overlapping territorial claims in the South China Sea.
He said Malaysia's defence preparedness depended not only on its military assets and personnel, but also on trusted partners willing to help build its capabilities.
Japan's OSA programme provides security and defence assistance to partner countries, with Malaysia among its early recipients.

Khaled said stronger defence capabilities would enable Malaysia to contribute more effectively to regional security. He also stressed the importance of regular bilateral and multilateral military exercises, saying continuous training was essential to preparing personnel for operational demands.
5aebe2e509159f64: KUALA LUMPUR: The Defence Ministry is considering the establishment of an annual Veterans Day to honour the contributions and sacrifices of armed forces veterans.

Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the National Veterans Council had agreed to support the proposal, which would see the celebration held nationwide each year, subject to cabinet approval.

"The proposed celebration would provide an opportunity to strengthen public appreciation for military veterans and recognise their sacrifices and service to the country," he said in his speech at the 100th National General Assembly of the Armed Forces Veterans Association.

Khaled said the government remained committed to safeguarding veterans' welfare while shifting its approach from providing one-off assistance to empowering them through skills development, retraining, employment opportunities and entrepreneurship programmes.
"Assistance will continue to be provided to those in need. At the same time, we want to ensure veterans can become independent, generate income and build better lives after completing their service.

"The Armed Forces Veterans Association plays an important role as a strategic partner to the ministry and the Veterans Affairs Department, particularly in conveying veterans' concerns and ensuring they are informed of government assistance and development programmes," he said.

He said veterans should not be viewed merely as recipients of welfare assistance, but as individuals with valuable experience, skills and capabilities who could continue contributing to society and the country.

He called on the association to encourage more veterans to participate in reskilling programmes, skills certification initiatives and employment-matching schemes, including those implemented through the Veterans Entrepreneur and Skills Training Corporation (Perhebat).
"The ministry is also working with the Human Resources Ministry to ensure veterans receive appropriate training, qualifications and career opportunities.
"Veterans could also contribute to the country's Comprehensive Defence concept, or Hanruh, by promoting defence awareness, instilling patriotism and strengthening community resilience," he said.
He said the ministry was expanding opportunities for veterans through career-matching programmes and economic initiatives.
"Under the Harga Istimewa Tentera Sejahtera (HITS) campaign at Pernama outlets in military camps, veterans are eligible to purchase goods at discounts of up to 30 per cent.
"The ministry is also committed to involving veteran-owned businesses in the defence industry, according to their capabilities."

Khaled assured veterans that their welfare and needs would not be neglected, adding that contributions to the Warriors Fund, which supports veterans and their families, had increased from RM1.3 million in 2023/2024 to RM2.19 million in 2024/2025 and RM3.35 million in 2025/2026.
Collections for 2026/2027 had so far reached RM4.35 million.
He said the Armed Forces Veterans Association, which had 182,786 registered members with the Veterans Affairs Department, was among the country's oldest and largest veterans' organisations.
b18ed95a6c6b7e6f: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) leadership is aiming to broker a resolution to the political crisis in Perlis, seeking direct talks with Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah following his two-term suspension from Bersatu.

PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan confirmed that he has officially written to Abu Bakar to request an urgent meeting to navigate the fallout from the disciplinary sanction and safeguard the stability of the state administration, NST reported.

"The discussions will focus on resolving ongoing issues, as PAS still supports the state government despite not being part of the state administration," he told a press conference following the Himpunan dan Munajat Penyatuan Ummah gathering in Kota Bharu last night.

Takiyuddin, who also serves as PAS secretary-general, noted that while Bersatu's disciplinary board had frozen Abu Bakar's party rights, the embattled state chief technically remains a Bersatu member.
He noted that this restricts Abu Bakar from seeking refuge outside of Bersatu.
"He cannot join another party, otherwise it would be party-hopping," he said.

Abu Bakar, who also heads the Kangar Bersatu division, was handed a two-election-term suspension after the party's disciplinary tribunal found him guilty of constitutional breaches. The punitive action sparked renewed questions over the viability of his leadership in the country's smallest state.

The crisis comes despite a royal intervention in June, when the Raja of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Putra Jamalullail, decreed that Abu Bakar should be given the necessary space and latitude to administer Perlis until the conclusion of the state legislative assembly's current mandate.

That royal guidance followed a fractious internal revolt last December, when five Bersatu assemblymen teamed up with three rebel PAS lawmakers to withdraw confidence from then-menteri besar Mohd Shukri Ramli of PAS.

The resulting reshuffle saw Bersatu wrest the menteri besar post for Abu Bakar, prompting an aggrieved PAS leadership to pull out of the state executive council entirely and leave the administration operating without formal PAS representation in government.
765fd3294be83c37: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 24 — The younger brother of the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman, son of the late Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah, passed away at 1.20 am today at Gleneagles Hospital, Kuala Lumpur. He was 51.

According to a statement by the Comptroller of the Terengganu Royal Household, Datuk Mohd Sophian Abu Bakar, the remains of Tengku Baderul Zaman will arrive at Sultan Mahmud Airport in Kuala Nerus at 1.15pm aboard a special aircraft.
The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail, will receive the remains of the late Tengku Baderul Zaman.
The remains will be taken to the Balai Islam, Istana Syarqiyyah, for final respects before being laid to rest at the Royal Mausoleum of Masjid Al-Muktafi Billah Shah.
The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail, has declared three days of mourning commencing today, with the following dress protocol.

For Muslim men, a songkok wrapped with an inch of white cloth. For non-Muslim men, an inch of white cloth wrapped around the songkok, a three-inch-wide black cloth band around the left sleeve, and a black necktie.
For Muslim women, a white headscarf; for non-Muslim women, a three-inch-wide black cloth band around the sleeve.
Tahlil ceremonies will be held for three consecutive nights at the Balai Islam beginning tonight. — Bernama
4da81fe89f755a9a: KUALA LUMPUR: Negotiations over Perikatan Nasional's (PN) request for two additional seats in the upcoming Melaka state election have been left to the party leadership to decide.
Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said a decision on the matter would be made in the near future.

"I think we should leave that (the two seats) to the party to decide," he said at a press conference after the opening ceremony of the 100th National General Assembly of the Armed Forces Veterans Association.
Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said PN hoped to negotiate for two additional seats in the state election.

He said that although Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had announced that seven seats had been allocated to Pas, the final decision on seat distribution would be made by the Seat Negotiations Committee.
7edf20640e84065c: PETALING JAYA: Bekas pengerusi DAP Melaka, Damian Yeo akan memboikot kempen Pakatan Harapan (PH) bagi PRN Melaka pada 14 Nov ini susulan khabar angin berhubung kemungkinan persefahaman pilihan raya dengan Bersatu.
Bekas Adun Duyong itu berkata, beliau menemui seorang lagi bekas ketua DAP Melaka, Tey Kok Kiew, baru-baru ini di mana mereka membincangkan strategi PH bagi PRN akan datang.
"Tetapi, apabila saya mendapat tahu rancangan di bawah PH Plus mungkin melibatkan penyerahan kerusi Bemban kepada Bersatu, reaksi spontan saya ialah 'Lupakan saja, saya tarik diri'.

"Luka akibat ditikam dari belakang belum sembuh. Sesetengah pengkhianatan politik terlalu sukar untuk dilupakan, apatah lagi dimaafkan," katanya merujuk peranan Bersatu dalam kejatuhan kerajaan persekutuan dan kerajaan Melaka pimpinan PH pada 2020.
"Selepas dengar semua ini, saya telah membuat keputusan: Saya tarik diri. Tiada lagi politik. Tiada lagi kempen pilihan raya.
"Ada perkara lain lebih berfaedah untuk saya lakukan dalam hidup saya. Semoga berjaya kepada semua," kata Yeo dalam hantaran di Facebook.
Yeo dilantik menerajui DAP Melaka pada 2021 susulan peletakan jawatan Tey. Beliau melepaskan jawatan itu dua tahun kemudian.

Yeo yang juga peguam, dipilih sebagai Adun Duyong pada 2018 dengan majoriti 2,895 undi. Beliau kehilangan kerusi itu kepada Noor Helmy Abdul Halem daripada Umno pada PRN 2021 dengan majoriti tipis 200 undi.
PH Melaka menegaskan ia akan bertanding solo pada PRN akan datang, tetapi spekulasi berhubung persefahaman pilihan raya dengan Bersatu terus bertebaran.
Spekulasi ini semakin hangat susulan majlis makan malam antara pemimpin PH negeri dan Bersatu pada bulan lalu, walaupun wakil DAP tidak hadir.
94afe088f99bdd87: KUALA LUMPUR: Immigration officers detained 68 foreigners, including 47 Thai women working as guest relations officers (GROs), in a raid on a Jalan Ampang nightclub during Ops Gegar at midnight.
The operation turned physical briefly when officers scuffled with security guards before securing the premises. Some women attempted to flee when they spotted the enforcement team.
Kuala Lumpur Immigration director Datuk Hamsha Injau said 113 people were screened. The detainees comprised 47 Thai women, seven Thai men and 14 Bangladeshi men.

The women reportedly earned commissions of up to RM3,000 a night for entertaining patrons. Hamsha said the nightclub used special sashes and outfits to display the rates customers paid, ranging from RM100 to RM3,000.
"The highest rate went up to RM3,000, while others were priced at RM1,000, RM500 and as low as RM100, which were distributed as commissions to the women," he said.
Hamsha said the raid followed public complaints, intelligence shared by partner agencies and two months of surveillance by the department.
Besides live singing and dancing, the club offered private karaoke rooms where GROs entertained patrons.
A security guard, who said he had worked at the club for nearly eight years under different managements, said he did not know how long it had been operating.
Hamsha said most of the foreigners had entered Malaysia on social visit passes but were engaged in immoral activities.
Checks also found foreign workers with employment passes for other sectors, including cleaning and construction, working at the entertainment outlet.
"We (Immigration) would like to remind foreign workers in Malaysia to comply with their pass conditions. If the pass is for the construction sector, work at construction sites.

"Here, we found construction and cleaning pass holders working in an entertainment outlet. They clearly violated the conditions of their passes, and action is being taken under Section 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963," he said.
He said operations targeting foreigners abusing social visit passes would be intensified across the federal capital.
The detainees, aged between 20 and 55, were taken to the Bukit Jalil Immigration Depot. Five locals were issued witness summonses to assist investigations.
Also present during the operation were Kuala Lumpur Immigration deputy director (Control) Azhar Ahmad and enforcement officers from the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living.
573cfdc58769c95c: GEORGE TOWN: Penang chief minister Chow Kon Yeow has expressed confidence that the long-awaited Air Itam-Lim Chong Eu Expressway (LCE) bypass project will be completed by April next year before being opened to the public.
He said contractor Consortium Zenith Construction Sdn Bhd (CZC) had committed to completing the RM851 million project within the given timeframe.
As of Sept 30, the project progress rate was 93.19%.
"The number of working teams has been increased to speed up work and meet the targeted timeframe," Chow said at a press conference after visiting the project site at Gelugor.
He said the key components of the project, such as the construction of bridge structures and viaducts, had been completed.
The focus is now on follow-up work like connecting parapets, installing road barriers, and paving, which will begin at the end of this month.

"However, before this bypass is opened to users, this route must undergo a technical compliance inspection and a road safety audit to ensure that all technical standards and safety requirements are met."

The chief minister also sought to assure that the state government would not face a funding crunch following reports that there were no bidders for the auction of 2.44ha of land in Gurney Bay intended to finance the remainder of the project.
He said CZC would foot the remaining RM50 million needed to complete the project. In return, the state government will transfer ownership of several land lots in Gurney Bay to the firm.

The 5.7km bypass, the first project under the Penang Transport Master Plan, will connect Air Itam and Farlim directly to the LCE. It is expected to shorten travelling time and ease congestion along Green Lane and Jalan Masjid Negeri.
The project was awarded to CZC in September 2013. The bypass was initially slated for completion in 2025 but was delayed until next year.
98809a656bbfda74: PETALING JAYA, Oct 24 — MSI Malaysia unveiled the Prestige N16 Flip AI+, its first laptop powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark and the only 2-in-1 convertible device in the first wave of RTX Spark Windows laptops announced globally.
The model was first released at the Computer Exhibition (Computex) in Taiwan in June and was officially launched for pre-orders worldwide on October 8.
It debuted in Malaysia during a media showcase at Common Ground in Jaya One on Thursday.
At the heart of the Prestige N16 Flip AI+ is the NVIDIA RTX Spark, the world’s first system-on-chip to integrate an RTX GPU, purpose-built for on-device agentic AI, content creation and gaming.
MSI Malaysia Notebook Marketing Manager Chris Liao said the model is rapidly gaining clout in Malaysia, largely because it goes beyond raw AI performance and has robust security features.
“Since pre-orders opened earlier this month, the Prestige N16 Flip AI+ has already earned strong praise from international product reviewers.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The Prestige N16 Flip AI also has a dual-biometric security feature, pairing a fingerprint sensor with an IR camera for facial recognition. — Picture by Yusof Isa

“It also offers stronger sign-in security, pairing a fingerprint sensor with an IR camera for facial recognition, a dual-biometric combination that sets it apart from other RTX Spark laptops,” Liao said at the media showcase.
Liao said the Prestige N16 Flip AI+ also has a bundled MSI Nano Pen and a 360-degree flip design, allowing users to type, take notes, sketch or present in a tablet mode.
A new dawn for agentic AI
The Prestige N16 Flip AI+ is also the most well-rounded RTX Spark laptop that is set to welcome a new era for agentic AI, according to MSI Malaysia.
Agentic AI, or autonomous AI, refers to a type of artificial intelligence that runs independently to design, execute and optimise workflows with little or no human intervention.
Since AI models contain billions of parameters, they run fastest when the whole model fits in a laptop’s Graphic Processing Unit (GPU) memory.
When memory is too small, data spills into slower system memory and responses lag. A larger memory pool lets users run bigger, more capable models at full speed.
So, the Prestige N16 Flip AI+ comes in two configurations: the 64GB model and the 128GB model.
The 64GB model is suitable for AI developers, software engineers, data scientists and content creators working with local generative AI, AI coding and video editing and rendering.
The 128GB works best for those working with large AI models, running up to 70-billion and 100-billion parameters locally.
A Vapor Chamber and IntraFlow cooling system also keeps performance stable during long-running AI agents, model inference, and software development without thermal throttling.
Also on display: Vincent Van Gogh and Draco editions
Yesterday’s showcase also featured three other landmark models from MSI Malaysia:
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The limited-edition Prestige 14 Flip AI Vincent van Gogh model on display during a media showcase by MSI Malaysia at Jaya One in Petaling Jaya on October 22, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa

Prestige 14 Flip AI+ Vincent van Gogh Edition: A limited-edition 2-in-1 convertible from the MSI Artisan Collection inspired by Starry Night Over the Rhône and The Starry Night. Measuring only 11.9mm thin, the 1.37kg device also comes with Intel® Core™ Ultra processors, a 14-inch OLED display, and an exclusive van Gogh-inspired accessory bundle.

Titan 18 HX Dragon Edition Draco Epic: MSI’s 40th-anniversary limited-edition flagship gaming laptop, inspired by the Draco constellation and finished with precision metal etching. It is powered by the Intel® Core™ Ultra 9 290HX Plus and NVIDIA® GeForce RTX™ 5090 Laptop GPU, with a collector’s bundle including a commemorative coin.

Modern 14S AI+: A light, everyday AI laptop for students and professionals, with Intel® Core™ Ultra processors, a 14-inch OLED display, 1.38kg weight, and Office Home 2024 included, starting from RM4,499.
The Prestige N16 Flip AI+ is available through the MSI official e-store and MSI authorised partners.
All units come with a 3-year on-site warranty.
Customers who purchase the device by December 2026 are also eligible to redeem the MSI Care Plus package, which includes a one-year warranty extension and one year accidental damage protection.
For more information, visit the MSI e-store at https://msi.gm/MYPN16AIPLUS_eSTORE or MSI official website at https://msi.gm/MYPN16AIPLUS.
d512e5e958953c44: GEORGE TOWN: Bahasa Melayu has a bright future if its use is expanded through digital technology, creative content and economic opportunities, says Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
She said the national language must evolve alongside other world languages while retaining its role as a cornerstone of Malaysia's identity, cultural heritage and unity.

"I believe Bahasa Melayu has a bright future if we dare to change our approach and expand the spaces in which it is used," she said when launching the 2026 National Language Month at Padang Kota Lama.
Her speech was read out by Education Malaysia deputy director-general (Professionalism Development Sector) Datuk Amzan Abd Malek.
Fadhlina said language was closely linked to identity, enabling generations to inherit and transmit knowledge, history, values and culture, while reflecting the courtesy and maturity of society.

She said upholding Bahasa Melayu was not merely about preserving heritage, but also ensuring that the national language continued to function as a language of knowledge, communication and national identity.
"In this era of globalisation and a borderless digital world, Bahasa Melayu must continue to advance alongside other world languages to enhance the economic value of our national language," she said.
She said Bahasa Melayu should not be viewed solely as a symbol of national identity, but also as a language capable of contributing to innovation, knowledge creation and economic development.

Fadhlina said the challenge was to ensure the language remained relevant to younger generations, particularly Generation Alpha, who grew up in a digital environment shaped by smart technology, social media, audiovisual content and artificial intelligence (AI).
She said young people were exposed to language not only through textbooks and classrooms, but also through videos, digital games, animation, music, streaming content and online interactions.

"We cannot simply ask the younger generation to love Bahasa Melayu. We must make it a language they want to use, a language they are proud of and a language that enables them to achieve their aspirations," she added.

She said the national language needed a stronger presence in the digital landscape through quality content, creative animation, educational games, informative short-form videos, electronic publications and applications based on the latest technologies.

Such initiatives, she said, would help attract younger audiences while creating opportunities to expand the use of Bahasa Melayu in education, creative industries, technological innovation and the digital economy.
Fadhlina stressed the importance of equipping young people with the ability to use Bahasa Melayu accurately, effectively and responsibly, particularly when communicating online.

She said the Education Ministry would continue strengthening the position of Bahasa Melayu through policies, curriculum development and educational programmes, adding that efforts to uphold the national language could not depend on campaigns and public appeals alone.

She said the government had also emphasised digital technology and AI development under the 2027 Budget, including a commitment to mobilise ministries, agencies and educational institutions to contribute authentic, annotated digital-language data to Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka (DBP).

She said the initiative would help build the digital resources needed to expand the use of Bahasa Melayu in AI applications and other emerging technologies, ensuring the language could keep pace with developments in science, knowledge and economic activity.
e597fe70b20c6e28: LOS ANGELES: Jayson Tatum scored 36 points as the Boston Celtics defeated the New York Knicks 107-103 to leave the NBA champions waiting for their first win of the season on Friday.

Tatum, back at full fitness after missing most of last season with a ruptured Achilles, delivered a mesmerizing performance at the TD Garden to give Boston their first win of the campaign after an opening-day loss to Detroit.
The six-time NBA All-Star shot 14-of-26 from the field, including three three-pointers, with nine rebounds, seven assists and three steals.
Nine of Tatum's points came in the fourth quarter as the Knicks, who had trailed by as many as 12 points early in the final frame, closed to within one point.
Tatum's superb all-round display earned words of admiration from Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla.
"That was a really well-balanced game from JT on both ends, and you were able to kind of see his greatness," Mazzulla said after the home opener.
Tatum received scoring support from new signing Paul George and Neemius Queta, who both finished with 15 points apiece.
The Knicks were led by 22 points from Karl-Anthony Towns, with OG Anunoby and Miles McBride scoring 20 each. Knicks talisman Jalen Brunson chipped in with 19.
In other games Friday, the Minnesota Timberwolves stayed unbeaten with a 115-93 defeat of the Orlando Magic on the road.
Minnesota's new-look offense, with Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball working in tandem, produced a balanced scoring display that saw seven players finish in double figures.
Edwards and Jaden McDaniels each netted 15 points to top the scoring. Orlando fell to 0-2 with the loss.
Elsewhere, the Atlanta Hawks moved to 2-0 with a 128-81 drubbing of the Charlotte Hornets, with Jalen Johnson and Aaron Wiggins scoring 19 points each.
The Toronto Raptors are also unbeaten thanks to a 112-102 defeat of the Washington Wizards on the road.
Scottie Barnes scored 28 points for Toronto with RJ Barrett adding 23 and Kawhi Leonard 16.

Kyrie Irving's 24-point haul helped the Dallas Mavericks to a 121-105 defeat of the Indiana Pacers while the Milwaukee Bucks were left waiting for their first win of the campaign after falling 132-125 to the Chicago Bulls at home. -- AFP
abf936d939daf206: KUALA LUMPUR: The Old Paulians' Association (OPA) has denied allegations that student prefects handled or served alcohol at its centenary reunion dinner in Seremban on Sept 5.

In a statement today, OPA president Steven Chan described the allegations circulating on social media as baseless and malicious, saying they were intended to damage the reputations of the association and St Paul's Institution (SPI).
He said the dinner was a private alumni function held at Regent Hall, Seremban, outside school premises and after school hours.

The event, attended by about 1,600 alumni and distinguished guests, commemorated the association's centenary and raised funds to upgrade school infrastructure, improve educational facilities and support student welfare at SPI.

Chan said the prefects participated voluntarily with written parental consent, and their duties were limited to ceremonial protocols, registration, promoting commemorative merchandise and welcoming guests.

"At no point were students directed, permitted or pressured to touch, pour, dispense or serve alcoholic beverages," he said, adding that the prohibition had been stated in written briefing notes and reiterated verbally.
He also rejected claims that objections raised during briefings had been ignored, describing them as fabrications.
Chan said neither teachers nor prefects had taken part in rehearsal sessions before the event.
He added that prefects helped distribute ordinary Chinese tea during toasts to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan and the school.

"Any surface foam observed immediately upon pouring was merely natural aeration from tea, which dissipated within moments and cannot under any circumstances be construed as evidence of wine or alcoholic beverages," he said.
On Oct 22, Badrul Hisham Shaharin, better known as Chegubard, alleged that 25 student prefects from SPI had been instructed to serve alcoholic beverages during the Sept 5 reunion dinner.

In a Facebook post, he claimed Muslim and non-Muslim teachers had objected during rehearsals and briefing sessions, with complaints reportedly lodged through the Education Ministry's Public Complaints Management System (SISPAA). He alleged that the event proceeded despite the objections.

Chegubard also highlighted the presence of several DAP leaders at the dinner, including Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook, a former SPI student, Kepayang assemblyman Nicole Tan Lee Koon and former Rahang assemblyman Mary Josephine Pritam Singh.
The Old Paulians' Association also criticised the circulation of photographs and selected video footage without context, saying these could mislead the public.
8f55cabd25a9cb0e: PETALING JAYA: A former Melaka DAP chairman has decided to boycott Pakatan Harapan's campaign for the Nov 14 Melaka state election over talk of a possible electoral understanding with Bersatu.
Former Duyong assemblyman Damian Yeo said he recently met fellow former Melaka DAP chief Tey Kok Kiew, where they discussed PH's strategies for the upcoming state polls.
"But when I heard that the plan under PH Plus could involve giving up Bemban to Bersatu, my immediate reaction was, 'Forget it, I am out.'

"The wound from being stabbed in the back is still fresh. Some political betrayals are simply too difficult to forget, let alone forgive," he said, citing Bersatu's role in the collapse of the PH-led federal and Melaka governments in 2020.
"After hearing all this, I have made up my mind: I'm out. No more politics. No more election campaigns.
“I have better things to do with my life. All the best to everyone," Yeo said in a Facebook post.
Yeo was appointed Melaka DAP chief in 2021 following Tey's resignation. He stepped down from the post two years later.
A lawyer by profession, Yeo was elected Duyong assemblyman in 2018 with a majority of 2,895 votes. He lost the seat to Umno's Noor Helmy Abdul Halem in the 2021 polls by a meagre 200 votes.
Melaka PH has insisted that it will contest in the upcoming state election on its own, but speculation of an electoral understanding with Bersatu persists.
This was further fuelled by a dinner between state PH and Bersatu leaders last month, although DAP representatives were not present.
1c2ecf5abe20e223: WASHINGTON: US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Friday called for Cubans to make "discreet" contact with the American intelligence services as Washington seeks to force an end to the island's communist government.
For months, President Donald Trump and other senior US officials have openly hinted at a military intervention or takeover of Cuba, ramping up economic, political and legal pressure on the country.
"To those who seek to create positive change in Cuba -- now is the time," Rubio said on social media.
"The disappointment of failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few; seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete partnership with the CIA."

271d3ce4761c9ac8: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian police are working with their Indonesian counterparts to establish whether a drug syndicate operating in Malaysia was involved in the attempted smuggling of 1.16 tonnes of ketamine hydrochloride aboard a tanker seized in Indonesian waters.

The Mongolian-flagged tanker, MT Global 168, which Indonesian authorities identified as belonging to Malaysian company Makmur Marine Petroleum, was intercepted off Tanjung Balai Asahan, North Sumatra, on Oct 20.
Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said Malaysian police were informed of the seizure by Indonesian authorities yesterday.
He said the operation uncovered 58 sacks containing 1,160 packages of ketamine hydrochloride, weighing a total of 1.16 tonnes.
"NCID will remain in close contact with the Indonesian National Police to obtain further details of the case and exchange relevant intelligence.
"We will also seek information to determine whether any members of drug syndicates operating in Malaysia were involved," he said when contacted today.

Hussein said preliminary information received from Indonesian authorities indicated that the tanker had departed from a docking facility in Pasir Gudang, Johor, before stopping at Port Klang to refuel.
"The vessel then headed towards the Andaman Sea, where it was believed to have conducted a ship-to-ship transfer of cargo in international waters.
"The tanker's movements had raised suspicions after it was detected displaying unusual sailing patterns between Oct 14 and 18.
"The vessel was believed to have switched off its Automatic Identification System (AIS) for three days in an attempt to evade detection," he said.
Hussein added that authorities had also detected suspicious circular movements off Thailand's western coast before the tanker headed towards the Andaman Sea.
He said eight crew members were detained following the seizure, comprising seven Indonesian men aged between 25 and 71 and a 42-year-old Chinese national.
The 57m tanker bears the Mongolian flag, he added.
Meanwhile, Indonesian news portal Justisio reported that Indonesian police had identified Johor-based Makmur Marine Petroleum as the company under which the tanker was registered.
According to the report, Indonesian police chief General Suyudi Ario Seto disclosed the company's identity during a press conference at Belawan Port in North Sumatra yesterday.
The report said Indonesian investigators had been monitoring the vessel since August following intelligence suggesting suspicious activities linked to international drug trafficking.
Suyudi was quoted as saying that the syndicate had also resorted to changing the vessel's name to avoid detection.
He said investigators were examining the possible involvement of corporate entities and individuals controlling the international trafficking network.
The Indonesian authorities have named all eight detained crew members as suspects.
The report also quoted Suyudi as saying that the seized drugs were worth an estimated 3.48 trillion rupiah (approximately RM800 million) and could have affected 5.8 million people.
Indonesian authorities are continuing investigations into the ownership and operation of the vessel, as well as the individuals believed to be behind the trafficking operation.

Hussein said NCID would continue exchanging intelligence with Indonesian police as investigations progressed, particularly to establish whether the shipment had any links to Malaysia-based drug trafficking networks.

41074d45858a23ab: SYDNEY: A 7.2 magnitude earthquake off Vanuatu triggered a tsunami warning on Saturday, the Pacific Tsunami Warning Centre said.

92bd530e373e1ff8: KUALA LUMPUR: Seramai 68 warga asing ditahan dalam serbuan Jabatan Imigresen Malaysia (JIM) di sebuah pusat hiburan di Jalan Ampang, awal pagi tadi.

In Negeri Sembilan, other places affected were Nilai (167) and Port Dickson (152). Other parts of Johor also recorded unhealthy air quality, namely Pasir Gudang (164), Batu Pahat (163), Tangkak (162), Kluang (159), Pengerang (157), Segamat (155) and Kota Tinggi (115).

Most parts of the Klang Valley continued to struggle with haze, with the API at 161 in Batu Muda (Sentul), 151 in Cheras and Putrajaya, 117 in Petaling Jaya and 107 in Klang.
Moderate API readings were meanwhile recorded in Banting (98), Johan Setia near Klang (98), Shah Alam (96) and Kuala Selangor (74).

API readings of between zero and 50 are categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and 301 and above as hazardous.
cd59aeab0f594260: PETALING JAYA: Kesukaran membuktikan pihak bertanggungjawab terhadap kebakaran di luar negara tidak sepatutnya menghalang Malaysia daripada menggubal undang-undang khusus bagi menangani jerebu rentas sempadan, kata pakar.

Pensyarah Jabatan Kejuruteraan Air dan Alam Sekitar Universiti Teknologi Malaysia, Mohd Fadhil Md Din, berkata akta baharu atau pindaan menyeluruh kepada Akta Kualiti Alam Sekeliling 1974 perlu dipertimbangkan bagi mengatasi jurang penguatkuasaan.
“Kita memerlukan rantaian bukti yang menghubungkan kebakaran, pihak bertanggungjawab, pergerakan asap dan pencemaran di Malaysia,” katanya kepada FMT.
Katanya, titik panas yang dikesan melalui satelit hanya petunjuk awal dan tidak mencukupi untuk membuktikan siapa yang melakukan pembakaran.
“Sebaliknya, data itu perlu disokong maklumat pemilikan tanah, aktiviti di lokasi kebakaran dan analisis pergerakan asap,” katanya.
Pakar undang-undang antarabangsa, Salawati Mat Basir, turut menyokong keperluan akta khusus kerana undang-undang sedia ada terhad kepada pembakaran terbuka dalam Malaysia.
“Akta Kualiti Alam Sekeliling 1974 hanya efektif untuk pembakaran terbuka yang berlaku dalam sempadan Malaysia,” katanya daripada Fakulti Undang-undang Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia.

Salawati berkata, siasatan perlu mengenal pasti pemilik dan pengendali kawasan kebakaran, termasuk kemungkinan penglibatan syarikat Malaysia melalui anak syarikat atau rantaian bekalan di luar negara.
“Kita perlu kenal pasti sama ada syarikat tempatan mempunyai rantaian bekalan atau anak syarikat di sana, supaya kita dapat mengenal pasti siapa yang berada di belakangnya,” katanya.

Fadhil berkata, Malaysia juga perlu memperkukuh kerjasama dengan Indonesia untuk mendapatkan maklumat pemilikan tanah, pengendali kawasan dan rekod kebakaran, kerana pihak berkuasa Malaysia tidak boleh menjalankan penguatkuasaan secara unilateral di negara lain.

Kedua-dua pakar mengulas kenyataan Timbalan Menteri Sumber Asli dan Kelestarian Alam, Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh, kekurangan bukti untuk mengenal pasti punca pencemaran dan pihak bertanggungjawab menjadi cabaran utama Malaysia dalam menggubal akta khusus jerebu rentas sempadan.

Beliau berkata, maklumat seperti koordinat kebakaran, pemilikan tanah dan pihak yang menjalankan aktiviti di kawasan terlibat perlu dikenal pasti, termasuk bukti mengaitkan kebakaran itu dengan jerebu di Malaysia.
Bagaimanapun, katanya Malaysia akan meneruskan kerjasama diplomatik dengan Indonesia serta usaha melalui Perjanjian Asean Mengenai Pencemaran Jerebu Rentas Sempadan.

Malaysia sebelum ini pernah mempertimbangkan undang-undang khusus bagi menangani jerebu rentas sempadan, namun cadangan itu tidak diteruskan pada 2020 selepas kerajaan ketika itu mengambil kira kebolehlaksanaan penguatkuasaan, hubungan diplomatik serta kesukaran mendapatkan bukti daripada negara lain.

Pada 2023, kerajaan sekali lagi memutuskan untuk tidak membentangkan rang undang-undang berkenaan selepas mengambil kira pandangan Jabatan Peguam Negara dan pakar undang-undang mengenai kesukaran mendakwa kesalahan yang berlaku merentasi sempadan.
Kerajaan kemudian menjelaskan ia tidak menutup sepenuhnya kemungkinan memperkenalkan undang-undang sedemikian.

d9a5df34a7dd9973: NEW YORK, Oct 24 — Oil prices rose to their highest levels since late April on Friday, with benchmark crude contract Brent North Sea climbing above US$116 (RM474) a barrel as the Middle East conflict raged on.
Global markets were contending “with concerns around surging oil prices and the sustainability of AI spending,” noted AJ Bell’s head of financial analysis Danni Hewson.

“Escalating tensions in Ukraine and the prospect of increased energy demand as the northern hemisphere heads into the winter months are only adding to the upwards pressure on oil and gas prices,” Hewson added.
The benchmark international oil contract, Brent crude for December, rose more than 3 per cent to US$116.72 (RM476.63) per barrel.
The benchmark US contract, West Texas Intermediate, jumped 3.8 per cent to US$103.27 (RM421.70) a barrel.
Wall Street’s main indices spent most of the day in negative territory. The Dow finished down 1.2 per cent, more than the 0.2 per cent retreat in the Nasdaq, reversing its trend in recent sessions.
“Today everyone appears to be rotating back into the stuff they rotated out of yesterday,” Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at online trading and investing platform IG.
“No one wants to be caught holding risk over the weekend,” he added.
European stock markets mostly dropped following some poorly-received earnings from Gucci parent Kering and Swedish group Volvo Cars.
Asian equity indices closed out the week mixed as technology companies managed to claw back some of the week’s hefty losses.

Rising energy prices have influenced movements across stock markets in recent days along with developments in the AI sector as investors have become more leery of massively expensive capital spending outlays for data centres.
“People are now looking at the cap ex as a liability and that’s different from six months ago,” said Joseph Zidle, chief market strategist at Cresset Capital.
Gucci, Volvo
Kering shed more than 16 per cent on Friday after the French luxury group published results that failed to reassure investors about a turnaround at its key Gucci brand.
Volvo Cars meanwhile plunged more than 24 per cent after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss.
In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor (RM2.1 billion) savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally.

Aside from energy markets, AI and earnings next week, focus will fall firmly on interest-rate meetings for the US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank, as well as an update on US economic growth data. — AFP

558fcb3948ca1986: From the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah Before I begin, I would like to congratulate Muzium Negeri Pahang on its 50th anniversary, its Golden Jubilee.

On this occasion, I remember with gratitude my late father-in-law, Almarhum Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah, who made Istana Kota Beram available to become a museum. That decision gave our heritage a home, and the museum has come a very long way since then.
So has its director.

I still remember Dato' Farid, the Dato Setia Jasa, as a skinny young man, fresh out of university. To me, he was practically a little boy. Today, he has grown in experience, confidence and wisdom, and acquired a few white hairs along the way.
I hope the museum deserves most of the credit for his wisdom, and that I am not entirely responsible for the white hairs!
But seriously, Farid has grown with this museum. I congratulate him on the ideas, dedication and vision he has brought to it, and on the ideas and vision he continues to have.
Our museum is increasingly talked about, and that makes me proud.

A museum must keep moving. It should inform and welcome people. Its exhibitions should change, giving visitors something new to discover and a reason to return. It should attract families, students, scholars and people who may never have thought that a museum was a place for them.
It should make people feel that their history belongs to them.
That is what I believe Muzium Pahang has worked hard to achieve.
My thanks also go to the staff whose work makes all this possible, and to the Pahang State Government for understanding our ambitions and continuing to support us.
Although, with a self-confessed control freak as the museum’s royal patron, perhaps they have not always had much choice!

This is also where a royal consort has work to do. Alongside the Sultan’s responsibilities, there is a contribution we can make through supporting our heritage, encouraging its practitioners and helping ensure that what we have inherited reaches another generation.
For me, that work comes from love. Patronage means taking an interest, listening, learning and being willing to sit with the people doing the work. Sometimes, quite literally, on the floor.
To everyone who has helped this museum reach its Golden Jubilee, thank you.
I must also confess that I feel rather humbled standing before so many distinguished scholars, each a master in his or her field.
And yes, a little nervous.

This is a subject about which many of you have spent your professional lives thinking and writing. I come before you with my own experience, my research and a great love for what I have been studying.
I have also realised that this seminar is being conducted in Malay, and I have prepared my keynote in English.
I do have a Malay translation. But I find that the English version allows me to express some of these thoughts more naturally.
Dato' Farid once told me, “Tuanku, speak in your mother tongue.”
I told him, “Yes, that is exactly what I am doing. My mother is English!”

There are thoughts that come to me more readily in English, and others that find their expression in Malay. So please allow me to speak in the language in which I can best share these reflections with you. And if some Malay finds its way in, that too is part of how I think.
This seminar has a very special place in my heart because it concerns a subject that has become so important to me: the Hukum Kanun of the Malay world, our Laws.
Through the Hukum Kanun Pahang, I discovered history. But I also discovered something within myself.

It challenged me, gave direction to my curiosity and helped me recognise what I was capable of achieving through study. For me, the work I have done on the Hukum Kanun Pahang is my greatest personal achievement.
It has changed the way I see things.

These days, whatever I am watching, reading or discussing, I seem to find myself comparing it with the Hukum Kanun Pahang. My family must sometimes wonder whether I can still have a conversation without bringing it into the discussion.
But that is what happens when a subject takes hold of your mind and your heart. You begin to recognise connections you had not seen before.
I thank Allah for leading me to that discovery, and for the opportunity to learn from it.
The keynote I am about to share grew from one such connection.
Before Tun Abdul Razak Hussein became Prime Minister, he was already a Shahbandar.

Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah holds a master’s degree from the International Institute of Islamic Thought and Civilisation (ISTAC), International Islamic University Malaysia, and is currently a PhD candidate at ISTAC-IIUM.

feb73f849ef2d58e: From Ravinder Singh
While education minister Fadhlina Sidek accurately stated that school caning was still legally allowed, current disciplinary frameworks are clearly falling short.
The regulations meant to ensure a safe and conducive learning environment have not prevented a severe decline in student behaviour, culminating in tragic instances of fatal school violence.
This crisis raises a critical question: have our existing school discipline rules completely failed?
The road to hell begins with good intentions

The Education (School Discipline) Regulations 1959 of Malaysia governs student discipline and corporal punishment in public schools. The red tape that schools must comply with in using the cane makes caning totally useless.

Only the head teacher or a designated teacher can use the cane, not the class teacher; caning must be done privately; another teacher must be present as a witness; details such as the child’s name, offence, punishment, date and time must be recorded.
As the then assistant headmaster of SK Tunku Abdul Halim in Alor Setar, I witnessed a dramatic shift in our school’s trajectory.

It was the premier primary school in northern Kedah during the 1950s and 1960s, but by 1990, when I took charge, it had become one of the worst. Faced with this crisis, I had two choices: allow the decay to continue or use the cane on my own terms to restore order.
I chose to do it my way, even though it bypassed standard disciplinary regulations. The approach worked, and I want to share that experience here.
Mayhem reigned in this school. Unbearable noise, unsightly litter everywhere, teachers screaming at children, children leaving classrooms and loitering, pushing and shoving at the canteen.

I was in total disbelief when the school head said at a staff meeting that “here we practice democracy”. This was clearly directed at me for controlling the “democracy” that children had been given the freedom to practice and pull the school down into the gutter.
Judicious use of the cane worked a miracle

Having given teachers a set of my own “classroom and child management rules” to be strictly implemented, I started my daily two rounds of corridor walking with a cane in hand for on-the-spot shock-giving to the brain to trigger re-wiring of the bad behaviour connections to good.
Of the 600 plus children in this boys’ school, hardly 10% needed the cure. The rest got the clear message that rules had to be obeyed; their previous “democratic” ways were not acceptable to me.
A light cane is most effective during early childhood, that is in pre-school and primary school, which is the critical habit-forming age. Not every child requires it.
However, for those who do, the physical sting serves as a necessary shock, breaking negative behavioural patterns and prompting them to re-evaluate their actions.
It works the same way that cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) does to shock the heart to start functioning again. Like CPR, the cane must be administered immediately after the event, without delay.
The cane was used only on the palms. One parent confronted me as his Year 3 son had a cane mark on his wrist because the boy had pulled his hand away.
“Do you have the authority to cane children?”
“Yes,” I said, as I told him I would not allow his son to disrupt a class of over 30, running around and pulling other children’s books and pencils while they did their work.
He could take his son to another school if he so wished. The son was soon back in school, a changed person. I set the standard, the parents followed.

On the first school day of the new year, I had a dialogue with the parents in the hall. I reminded them of this school’s excellent status in the 1950s and 1960s, and its shameful status now, all because discipline had not been strictly maintained.
To achieve good academic performance, the prerequisite was good discipline. If teachers had to use the cane to restore discipline, it was for the good of the children.
They gave me unanimous support, and I never had an issue with any of them as long as I was there. Teachers were happy they could conduct lessons with children paying attention.

When I left one and a half years later it took just one week for “democracy” to return to the school. It was heartbreaking that no one could continue maintaining the discipline that I had taken so much trouble to restore within three months of taking charge.
False theories surrounding child disciplining issues
There is not a single study of an actual hands-on use of the cane in real-life situations like I did. All other “studies” are based on the results of wrongful use of the cane.
This is like compiling a list of botched medical surgeries and concluding that surgeries can cause deaths and paralysis and therefore should be banned.
In my own way I proved that a light cane, properly used, is an excellent tool for maintaining discipline in primary school. Then, strict discipline has to be maintained in secondary schools.
The education ministry should not dismiss the “grandfathers’ way” of disciplining children. If schools set the discipline standard, parents will respect it and do their part.
When schools accept indiscipline, parents think that is normal and cannot accept when any teacher disciplines their child.
Get it right — every school must set and enforce strict discipline. Only when schools stop accepting indiscipline will parents take the discipline of their children seriously.
Ravinder Singh is an FMT reader.

b482ac6e1114a80c: Saya petik laporan Berita Harian siaran 22 Okt lalu mengenai ucapan Nik Muhammad Zawawi Salleh, Ahli Parlimen PAS bagi Pasir Putih, yakni ketika beliau membahas Rang Undang-undang Perbekalan 2027 di Parlimen. Beliau gesa kerajaan kurangkan pemberian bantuan tunai dan beri lebih tumpuan kepada usaha memperkasakan rakyat supaya mampu menjana pendapatan sendiri untuk jangka panjang. Ada yang saya setuju, dan ada tidak.

Kata Zawawi, kerajaan perlu mendidik rakyat supaya berusaha mencipta peluang dan bekerja untuk meningkatkan kehidupan. Bagi saya, rakyat tidak perlu diajar oleh kerajaan. Tidak perlu kerajaan berkhutbah menggesa rakyat 'cipta peluang' dan 'kerja' untuk tingkatkan tahap kehidupan, sebab sememangnya rakyat terutama golongan miskin tahu itu semua. Mereka tahu apa yang perlu dilakukan untuk survive dan tingkatkan kehidupan.
That's what they have been doing all this while.

Sememangnya rakyat sentiasa bekerja (dengan keras) serta mencari dan mengintai peluang untuk senang dan menikmati lebih kesenangan. They don’t need the government to lecture or teach what they have to do to improve their livelihood.

Berkata lagi Zawawi: "kalau kita ada peruntukan, rakyat kita bagi 'kail', jangan kita bagi 'ikan'". Umum faham yang dimaksudkan beliau. Benar ada pepatah Inggeris, "give a man a fish and you feed him for a day, teach a man to fish and you feed him for a lifetime".

Comedian terkenal, Trevor Noah, menambah "and it would be nice if you gave him a fishing rod". Zawawi got it right on this. Berikan 'kail' kepada rakyat bagi membolehkan mereka mendapat 'ikan' buat selama-lamanya.

Namun dalam menyatakan beri rakyat 'kail', Zawawi juga berkata, "kalau kita bagi subsidi, kita bagi 'ikan', dia mengajar rakyat ini malas". Maksudnya beliau menyamakan pemberian subsidi dengan pemberian 'ikan', dan buat rakyat malas. Ini pelik dan saya tidak setuju.

Bagaimana 'subsidi' boleh dikaitkan dengan 'malas'? Subsidi ke atas barangan keperluan misalnya ialah bagi meringankan beban rakyat untuk memiliki barangan berkenaan, membolehkan rakyat mampu beli apa yang mereka perlu. Rakyat masih perlu bekerja untuk mendapat duit untuk membeli barangan yang disubsidi. Kata kuncinya 'beli', bukan percuma.

Walaupun barang dibeli pada harga lebih rendah daripada harga asal tanpa subsidi, tetapi hakikatnya kena beli. Untuk beli perlu duit. Untuk dapat duit, rakyat perlu bekerja. Jadi apabila rakyat bekerja, mereka bukan malas. Maka tidak adil dan tidak betul untuk kata subsidi buat rakyat malas. Jika ada pihak yang risau mengenai subsidi, it's the government kerana subsidi boleh membebankan.

Seterusnya Zawawi dipetik berkata: "kalau kita bagi duit, kalau dia boleh guna seminggu, seminggu habis". Money is meant to be spent. Kalau duit digunakan untuk beli barangan keperluan atau perbelanjaan penting seperti tambang anak ke sekolah dan buku tambahan maka tidak ada dosanya duit habis dalam seminggu. Mereka bukan joli sehingga duit habis.

Zawawi juga berkata: "tapi kalau kita bagi periuk, kuali, kita bagi mesin, kita bagi alat, dia boleh gunakan alat ini bertahun-tahun dan mungkin dia boleh bangkit dengan baik". Betul kata-kata itu. Bagaimanapun apa yang boleh dilakukan dengan kuali, periuk, mesin tanpa bahan memasak misalnya?

Bagaimana mahu perolehi bahan-bahan itu? Pastinya terpaksa dibeli. Macam mana mahu beli? Perlu duit. Ertinya bantuan duit tetap diperlukan untuk beri si penerima kuali, periuk dan mesin a head start. Perlu diingat juga keluar rumah untuk pergi kerja pun memerlukan duit. Nothing is free, my friend, apa lagi pada zaman ini.

Untuk berlaku adil, perlu dinyatakan Zawawi tidak menafikan terdapat golongan memerlukan bantuan kewangan termasuk ibu tunggal, yang mempunyai ramai anak dan sukar bekerja selain golongan sakit serta orang kurang upaya. This is stating the obvious.
Artikel ini ialah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
187dded282ab3a33: PARIS: Moody's spared France a credit rating downgrade on Friday, easing pressure on a government struggling to contain social unrest and shore up its strained finances.
Moody's said it had concluded a periodic review of its rating, leaving it at Aa3, which has carried a negative outlook since last October.

Bond markets had been pricing in a downgrade, which would have brought Moody's in line with Standard & Poor's and Fitch, which moved earlier as France struggled to rein in its public finances after a 2024 snap election produced a hung parliament and political paralysis.

The French finance ministry said in a statement that the fact Moody's kept its rating unchanged reflected the "credibility of the budget the government has put forward in the 2027 finance bill, which is designed to keep our public finances on the path to recovery."
The government is struggling to pass the bill in parliament, where opposition parties could refuse to compromise, reject the legislation and topple the government in a no-confidence vote.
"The Aa3 rating assumes that a deficit-reducing budget for 2027 will be adopted, while financing costs and social tensions will abate somewhat in the next few months," Moody's said in a statement.

French borrowing costs already exceed those of lower-rated peers such as Italy, as investors fret over the budget deficit -- one of the eurozone's biggest -- and a presidential election on April 18 and May 2 next year that polls suggest the far right could win.
TV images of weekend protests descending into riots and looting underscore the political difficulty of pushing budget cuts through.

That helped push the risk premium on French government debt over safe-haven German bonds to its highest in 15 years on Thursday, while France's benchmark 10-year bond yield hit 5.14%, its highest level since July 2002.
Moody's said earlier this month that the French government's ability to overcome "fragmentation in parliament" would be the key factor for its next rating move.

That task looks harder after violent protests over underfunded schools escalated last weekend into riots during mass cost-of-living demonstrations. The government has refused to release more school funding or raise the minimum wage, and further protests are planned for Saturday.

In parliament, the lower house has scrapped some key savings measures in the 2027 budget, which targets a deficit of 5% of output versus 5.4% this year. Opposition parties show little appetite for compromise before the election, scrapping some proposed cuts while adding spending.

"You want to wait and see how the narrative evolves over the next six months into the election. That's going to have a more meaningful impact on the spread," said Rushabh Amin, a portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments.

Pressure on French debt could grow after the presidential vote if Moody's, S&P and Fitch all cut France to BBB -- just above junk status -- potentially forcing sales by those investors with rating limits, said Mike Bell, head of market strategy at RBC BlueBay Asset Management.
"That's where it could really start to get more ugly," he added.
